classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: vertical_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density
items.description:
Vertical Pfirsch–Schlüter current density is the signed height-axis
projection of the neoclassical return current that restores current
continuity in toroidal confinement.
items.documentation:
Vertical Pfirsch–Schlüter current density is the height-axis projection of
the [Pfirsch–Schlüter current-density
vector](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density). This neoclassical return
current restores local current continuity by balancing the divergence of the
pressure-gradient diamagnetic current in toroidal confinement.

The projection is defined by:

$$
j_{\mathrm{PS},Z} = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{PS}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{Z}}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{PS},Z}$ is the vertical Pfirsch–Schlüter current density,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{PS}}$ is the Pfirsch–Schlüter current-density vector,
and $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the vertical unit vector parallel to the toroidal
symmetry axis. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity is the local edge-plasma contribution to [current
density](name:current_density) associated with the Pfirsch–Schlüter return
current, summed over participating charge carriers rather than resolved by
species or charge state. It is neither the total current density from all
mechanisms nor the magnitude of the Pfirsch–Schlüter current-density vector;
no flux-surface averaging is implied.

Unlike [parallel Pfirsch–Schlüter current
density](name:parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density), which projects
the same vector onto the local magnetic-field direction, this component
projects onto the fixed vertical direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the Pfirsch–Schlüter current-density vector
has a component in the direction of increasing vertical height $Z$.

items.name: z_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
items.description:
Signed Z component of the minor-axis unit vector defining the orientation of
an elliptic shatter cone in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the projection of the unit vector along an elliptic shatter
cone's minor geometric axis onto the Cartesian z direction.

The component is defined by

$$
u_{\mathrm{minor},z} = \mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{minor}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{minor}}$ is the unit vector directed along the
shatter cone's minor axis, $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit basis vector for
increasing $z$ in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$
frame, and $u_{\mathrm{minor},z}$ is their scalar projection.

This quantity applies only to the minor geometric axis of the shatter cone
and represents one Cartesian component, not the complete orientation vector,
its magnitude, or a component of the major axis. It is a signed component
and is not an aggregate over multiple axes or objects.

Together with the remaining Cartesian components, including the [x component
of the shatter-cone minor-axis unit
vector](name:x_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), it defines the
minor-axis orientation. It is distinct from the [z component of the
shatter-cone major-axis unit
vector](name:z_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), which describes the
other principal axis.

items.name: vertical_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport
items.description:
Vertical current density due to anomalous transport is the signed
conventional-charge flux along the toroidal symmetry axis attributed to
turbulent, nonclassical plasma transport.
items.documentation:
Vertical current density due to anomalous transport is the signed vertical
projection of the conventional electric-current contribution attributed to
turbulent, nonclassical plasma transport.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height along the toroidal
symmetry axis. The defining projection is

$$
j_Z = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{anom}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $j_Z$ is the vertical anomalous current density,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{anom}}$ is the vector [current density due to anomalous
transport](name:current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport), and
$\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along the symmetry axis toward
increasing $Z$.

This quantity is a local component of the anomalous contribution, not the
total vertical current density or a spatially integrated electric current.
Its direction is fixed by the symmetry axis, whereas [parallel current
density due to anomalous
transport](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport)
projects the same anomalous-current vector along the local magnetic field.

Sign convention: Positive when the anomalous conventional current flows
toward increasing $Z$.

items.name: source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion
items.description:
Source rate due to thermal fusion is the volume-integrated production rate
of a specified fusion-reaction product or source term generated by
thermonuclear reactions among thermal bulk ions. More specific names define
the emitted product or channel aggregation; the thermal qualifier excludes
fast-ion fusion contributions.
items.documentation:
Source rate due to thermal fusion is the volume-integrated production rate
of a specified fusion-reaction product or source term generated by
thermonuclear reactions among thermal, approximately Maxwellian ion
populations in the plasma. It is a parent concept for source rates whose
child names identify the produced particle or source component.

The source rate is defined by integrating the corresponding local
source-rate density over the plasma volume:

$$
S_{\mathrm{tf}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{p}}} s_{\mathrm{tf}}(\mathbf{x})\, dV
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{tf}}$ is the source rate due to thermal fusion,
$s_{\mathrm{tf}}$ is the local source-rate density due to thermal fusion for
the same specified product or source term, and $V_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the
plasma volume.

This parent does not by itself specify the reaction-product species,
fusion-reaction channel, or channel aggregation. For example, the [neutron
source rate due to thermal
fusion](name:neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion) specializes this
concept to neutron production. The thermal-fusion qualifier restricts the
contributing reactions to thermal bulk-ion fusion and excludes beam-target,
beam-beam, and other fast-ion fusion contributions.

items.name: poloidal_angle_of_flux_surface
items.description:
Poloidal angle at a point on a flux surface, measured about the magnetic
axis from the outward horizontal ray. It increases clockwise in the poloidal
cross-section, with major radius to the right and vertical height upward.
items.documentation:
Poloidal angle of flux surface

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the angle is
defined by:

$$
\theta = \operatorname{atan2}(Z_{\mathrm{axis}} - Z,\; R - R_{\mathrm{axis}})
$$

Here, $\theta$ is the poloidal angle at the point; $R$ and $Z$ are its major
radius and vertical height; and $R_{\mathrm{axis}}$ and $Z_{\mathrm{axis}}$
are the major radius and vertical height of the magnetic axis. The function
$\operatorname{atan2}$ is the quadrant-resolving two-argument inverse
tangent. The angle is undefined at the magnetic axis, where both arguments
vanish, and values differing by $2\pi$ represent the same direction.

The quantity applies pointwise to positions on a flux surface; it is not a
single angle for the entire surface and is not a surface average. It is a
geometric positional angle, distinct from a straight-field-line poloidal
angle. The [poloidal magnetic flux at a flux
surface](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_flux_surface) identifies the
surface, while this angle distinguishes positions around it. It uses the
same geometric convention as the [poloidal angle at a measurement
position](name:poloidal_angle_of_measurement_position), with the evaluation
locus here being a flux surface.

Sign convention: Positive when the angle increases clockwise from the
outward horizontal ray in the poloidal cross-section, with $R$ increasing to
the right and $Z$ increasing upward.

A surface formed by points sharing the same magnetic-flux label in a
nested-flux-surface configuration. Where $\psi(R, Z) = \mathrm{const}$,
$\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux.

items.name: toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part
items.description:
In-phase real coefficient of the toroidal magnetic-field perturbation
eigenfunction in the current-free vacuum surrounding the plasma, resolved
for one toroidal Fourier mode.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the real part of the toroidal component of the first-order
complex magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction in the current-free vacuum
surrounding the plasma. It is one component of the full [toroidal perturbed
vacuum magnetic field](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field) and
excludes the equilibrium field and perturbations within the plasma.

The real coefficient is defined from the complex toroidal perturbation by

$$
\delta B_{\phi,\mathrm{R}} = \operatorname{Re}\!\left[\delta B_\phi\right], \qquad \delta B_\phi = \delta\mathbf{B} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\delta\mathbf{B}$ is the complex first-order perturbed magnetic-field
vector, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector, and $\delta
B_{\phi,\mathrm{R}}$ is its real part. The projection is defined in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, and the quantity belongs to the
specified toroidal Fourier mode; its quadrature counterpart is the
[imaginary part of the toroidal perturbed vacuum magnetic
field](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part). In the
vacuum region, the perturbation is current-free and satisfies $\nabla \times
\delta\mathbf{B}=0$.

Sign convention: Positive when the toroidal perturbation component points in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_primary_x_point
items.description:
Signed vertical position of the primary magnetic X-point, the poloidal-field
null where separatrix branches meet, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ,
Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The primary X-point is the main poloidal magnetic-field null on the plasma
boundary, where separatrix branches meet. This quantity gives that point’s
vertical coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

$$
Z_{\mathrm{X,primary}} = \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{X,primary}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{Z}}
$$

Here, $Z_{\mathrm{X,primary}}$ is the vertical coordinate of the primary
X-point, $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{X,primary}}$ is its position vector relative
to the coordinate origin, and $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the vertical unit vector
of the cylindrical frame.

The locus is specifically the primary, or main, boundary X-point rather than
an unspecified or secondary X-point. This is a pointwise geometric
coordinate with no spatial averaging, surface integration, population
aggregation, or species dependence; it excludes the radial coordinate of the
same point.

The generic [vertical coordinate of an
X-point](name:vertical_coordinate_of_x_point) represents the same signed Z
coordinate without restricting the locus to the primary X-point, while the
[radial coordinate of an X-point](name:radial_coordinate_of_x_point)
supplies the corresponding major-radius coordinate.

Sign convention: Positive when the primary X-point lies in the direction of
increasing vertical coordinate $Z$.

items.name: nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket_shield
items.description:
Nuclear heating power deposited in the breeder blanket shield by neutron and
gamma interactions within the shield material. It excludes externally
applied, incident, or surface heat loads not produced by nuclear energy
deposition in the shield.
items.documentation:
Nuclear heating power deposited in the breeder blanket shield is the rate at
which neutron- and gamma-induced interactions deposit energy as heat within
the shield portion of a breeder blanket. The shield is the shielding
structural region of the breeder blanket, distinct from the blanket as a
whole and from its breeding or multiplier regions.

The quantity is the volume integral of the local nuclear heat-deposition
rate over the shield region:

$$
P_{\mathrm{nuc,shield}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{shield}}} q'''_{\mathrm{nuc}}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{nuc,shield}}$ is the nuclear heating power of the breeder
blanket shield, $V_{\mathrm{shield}}$ is the volume occupied by the shield
portion of the breeder blanket, $q'''_{\mathrm{nuc}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the
local nuclear heat-deposition rate from neutron and gamma interactions at
spatial position $\mathbf{r}$, and $dV$ is an infinitesimal volume element.

The scope is the aggregate shield contribution, integrated over all material
volume identified as breeder-blanket shield material and summed over the
nuclear energy deposited there by neutrons and gamma radiation. It excludes
heating deposited in non-shield breeder-blanket regions, heating in adjacent
structures, and externally applied, incident, or surface heat loads that are
not generated by nuclear interactions within the shield material.

This quantity is a component of the [nuclear heating power of the breeder
blanket](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket). It is distinguished
from [nuclear heating power of a breeder blanket
module](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket_module) and [nuclear
heating power of a breeder blanket
layer](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket_layer), which restrict
the same nuclear heat-deposition concept to their respective subregions; for
any disjoint partition of the same shield region, the aggregate shield value
equals the sum over the corresponding subregion contributions.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_parallel_current_density
items.description:
Flux-surface-averaged parallel current density is the surface average of
conventional current density dotted with the magnetic field, divided by a
single global reference toroidal field.
items.documentation:
Flux-surface-averaged parallel current density is the signed field-aligned
contribution of the total plasma current density, averaged over a closed
magnetic flux surface with magnetic-field weighting.

The defining relation is

$$\langle f\rangle = \oint f\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|$$

where $j_\parallel^{\mathrm{FS}}$ denotes this averaged parallel current
density, $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic flux labeling the surface,
$\mathbf{j}$ is the total conventional plasma [current
density](name:current_density), $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field
vector, and $B_0$ is the nonzero signed global reference toroidal magnetic
field. The brackets denote the normalized flux-surface average, weighted by
the inverse magnitude of the poloidal magnetic-flux gradient. The same $B_0$
applies to every surface; it is not a surface-dependent magnetic-field
magnitude.

The quantity includes all plasma current-carrying populations and mechanisms
and aggregates over the complete selected closed surface. It is not
restricted to a particular current-drive mechanism and is not a pointwise
current density.

The pointwise [parallel current density](name:parallel_current_density) is
$j_\parallel=\mathbf{j}\cdot\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$, where $|\mathbf{B}|$
is the magnetic-field magnitude. Consequently, this quantity equals $\langle
j_\parallel|\mathbf{B}|\rangle_\psi/B_0$, not generally $\langle
j_\parallel\rangle_\psi$. The [constraint-position
member](name:flux_surface_averaged_parallel_current_density_at_constraint_position)
evaluates the same quantity on the magnetic surface selected by a specified
constraint position; no such locus is prescribed here.

The reference field is positive toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in
the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius
and $Z$ is vertical height.

Sign convention: Positive when
$\langle\mathbf{j}\cdot\mathbf{B}\rangle_\psi$ is positive for a reference
toroidal field directed toward increasing $\phi$, or negative for a
reference field directed toward decreasing $\phi$.

items.name: alfven_frequency_real_part
items.description:
Oscillation angular frequency, the real part of the complex angular
frequency of the local shear Alfvén continuum at a specified position across
magnetic flux surfaces for a single toroidal mode number.
items.documentation:
Oscillation angular frequency is the real part of the complex angular
frequency of a local shear-Alfvén continuum root. It gives the signed
oscillatory component of that continuum branch at a specified position
across magnetic flux surfaces for one toroidal mode number.

The real part is defined from the complex continuum angular frequency by:

$$
\omega_{\mathrm{A,r}} = \operatorname{Re}\!\left(\Omega_{\mathrm{A}}\right)
$$

where $\omega_{\mathrm{A,r}}$ is this oscillation angular frequency,
$\Omega_{\mathrm{A}}$ is the [complex Alfvén
frequency](name:alfven_frequency), and $\operatorname{Re}$ denotes the
real-part operator.

The scope is one local shear-Alfvén continuum root at one position across
the magnetic flux surfaces and one toroidal mode number; it is not an
average, envelope, or sum over roots, positions, or mode numbers. The
toroidal mode number $n$ is the integer Fourier index of variation in
toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed
from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height. This quantity excludes
global eigenmode frequencies and continua not belonging to the shear-Alfvén
branch.

The [complex Alfvén frequency](name:alfven_frequency) decomposes into this
quantity and its imaginary companion as $\Omega_{\mathrm{A}} =
\omega_{\mathrm{A,r}} + i\gamma_{\mathrm{A}}$, where $i$ is the imaginary
unit and $\gamma_{\mathrm{A}}$ is the [Alfvén-frequency imaginary
part](name:alfven_frequency_imaginary_part), representing growth or damping
under the same complex-frequency convention. The signed value
$\omega_{\mathrm{A,r}}$ identifies the selected real branch; the
non-negative magnitude $|\omega_{\mathrm{A,r}}|$ is an unsigned oscillation
rate and is not this quantity. The branch sign follows the phase convention
that the oscillatory perturbation is proportional to
$\exp[i(n\phi-\Omega_{\mathrm{A}}t)]$, where $t$ is time.

Sign convention: Positive when the temporal phase of the oscillatory factor
$\exp[-i\Omega_{\mathrm{A}} t]$ decreases with increasing time, so for
positive toroidal mode number $n$ the corresponding constant-phase surface
moves toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with the position on the flux surface
otherwise held fixed.

items.name: neutron_emissivity_due_to_fusion
items.description:
Local volumetric rate of neutron production from all included fusion
reactions, giving the spatial distribution of fusion neutron emission per
unit volume at each point in the plasma.
items.documentation:
The neutron emissivity due to fusion $\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm{fus}}$ is the
local number of neutrons produced per unit volume per unit time from all
included fusion reactions. Each contributing neutron-producing branch adds
its local neutron yield, so this quantity is the reaction-channel-aggregated
fusion neutron source rather than a single-channel contribution.

For included binary fusion reaction branches, the emissivity is defined by:

$$
\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm{fus}} = \sum_{(\{a,b\},r)\in\mathcal{C}} \nu_{ab,r}^{(n)} \frac{n_a n_b}{1+\delta_{ab}} \langle \sigma v \rangle_{ab,r}
$$

where $\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm{fus}}$ is the neutron emissivity due to
fusion, $\mathcal{C}$ is the set of included unordered reacting-species
pairs and fusion reaction branches, $a$ and $b$ identify the reacting ion
species, $r$ identifies a reaction branch, $\nu_{ab,r}^{(n)}$ is the number
of neutrons produced by one reaction in that branch, $n_a$ and $n_b$ are the
local number densities of the reacting ion populations, $\delta_{ab}$ is the
Kronecker delta for identical reacting species, and $\langle \sigma v
\rangle_{ab,r}$ is the velocity-averaged fusion reactivity for that branch.

This quantity is local to each point in the plasma and is summed over the
included neutron-producing fusion branches and their reacting ion
populations. The factor $1+\delta_{ab}$ counts unordered pairs of identical
reactants once, so identical-population reactions such as
deuterium-deuterium are not double-counted. It represents neutron production
only; it excludes charged fusion products, radiation other than neutrons,
and the released fusion energy represented by
[power_density_due_to_fusion](name:power_density_due_to_fusion).

The related quantity emissivity_due_to_fusion is already restricted to
fusion neutron production; this quantity should not be interpreted as a
neutron-only component of a broader all-product emissivity. Single-channel
contributions are represented by
[deuterium_deuterium_emissivity_due_to_fusion](name:deuterium_deuterium_emissivity_due_to_fusion)
and
[deuterium_tritium_emissivity_due_to_fusion](name:deuterium_tritium_emissivity_due_to_fusion);
summing the included channel contributions gives this reaction-aggregated
emissivity. Volume integration of $\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm{fus}}$ gives
neutron_rate with the same reaction-channel aggregation.

items.name: vertical_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction
items.description:
Vertical current density due to ion–neutral friction is the signed
electric-charge flux contribution along the symmetry axis arising from
momentum exchange between plasma ions and neutrals.
items.documentation:
Vertical current density due to ion–neutral friction is the vertical
projection of the [current density due to ion–neutral
friction](name:current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction). It represents
the electric-current contribution attributable to frictional momentum
exchange between plasma ions and neutral particles.

The component is defined by

$$
j_Z = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $j_Z$ is this vertical current-density contribution,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the ion–neutral-friction current-density
vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector parallel to the toroidal
symmetry axis toward increasing height. The direction is defined in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is the distance
from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle, and $Z$ is the
vertical height.

This is a local contribution in a partially ionized plasma, without spatial
averaging or integration. It excludes contributions assigned to other
mechanisms and does not represent the total plasma [current
density](name:current_density). The [radial current density due to
ion–neutral
friction](name:radial_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction) is a
different projection of the same mechanism-resolved vector, rather than an
additional mechanism.

Sign convention: Positive when the ion–neutral-friction contribution carries
conventional electric current toward increasing vertical height $Z$.

items.name: vorticity
items.description:
Vorticity is the curl of the plasma bulk velocity field, measuring the
signed local angular rotation of fluid elements. It is the parent quantity
for radial, toroidal, vertical, and field-aligned projections of that curl.
items.documentation:
Vorticity is the curl of the plasma bulk velocity field and represents the
local rotational content of the single-fluid plasma flow. For solid-body
rotation it is twice the angular-velocity vector of a fluid element.

The vorticity field $\boldsymbol{\omega}$ is defined by the curl of the
plasma bulk velocity field:

$$
\boldsymbol{\omega} = \nabla \times \mathbf{v}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\omega}$ is the vorticity field, $\mathbf{v}$ is the
plasma bulk velocity, and $\nabla \times$ is the curl operator with
right-handed orientation.

The scope is the local magnetohydrodynamic plasma bulk-flow field at a point
in the plasma. The bare name carries no surface, volume, time, species, or
charge-state aggregation. It is not vorticity magnitude, flow shear, strain
rate, divergence, or magnetic-field-line twist.

The unqualified quantity is the parent for scalar directional projections of
the same curl. [Radial vorticity](name:radial_vorticity), [toroidal
vorticity](name:toroidal_vorticity), and [vertical
vorticity](name:vertical_vorticity) are projections onto $\hat{R}$,
$\hat{\phi}$, and $\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, respectively; [parallel vorticity](name:parallel_vorticity) is the
projection along the local magnetic-field direction. The bare name does not
designate a poloidal projection.

Sign convention: Positive when $\boldsymbol{\omega}$ has a positive
projection on the stated scalar direction: $+\hat{R}$, $+\hat{\phi}$, or
$+\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, or the
local magnetic-field direction for a field-aligned projection.

Related quantities: [poloidal_vorticity](name:poloidal_vorticity).

items.name: runaway_electron_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective runaway-electron convection velocity is the vector velocity
assigned to advective, non-diffusive transport of the runaway-electron
population. It denotes the full vector quantity; component or projection
quantities are specializations.
items.documentation:
Effective runaway-electron convection velocity is the vector velocity
assigned to the advective part of runaway-electron transport. It represents
non-diffusive motion of the runaway-electron population in a transport
representation, independent of any particular component or projection.

The convective contribution to the runaway-electron particle flux density is
defined by:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{\mathrm{RE}}^{\mathrm{conv}} = n_{\mathrm{RE}}\,\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{RE}}^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{\mathrm{RE}}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective
runaway-electron particle flux density, $n_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the
runaway-electron number density, and
$\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{RE}}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the runaway-electron
convection velocity.

This quantity excludes diffusive transport terms, source terms, and the
total runaway-electron particle flux density. Component or projection
quantities, such as the [perpendicular runaway-electron convection
velocity](name:perpendicular_runaway_electron_convection_velocity), are
specializations of this vector and do not redefine the parent quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component of
$\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{RE}}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ points in the positive sense of
that component's stated direction.

items.name: parallel_ion_current_density
items.description:
Parallel ion current density is the signed conventional electric-charge flux
carried by ions along the local magnetic field at a plasma-facing surface.
items.documentation:
Parallel ion current density at a plasma-facing surface is the signed
projection of the [ion current-density vector](name:ion_current_density)
onto the local magnetic-field direction.

The projection is defined by:

$$
j_{\parallel,i} = \hat{\mathbf{b}}\cdot\mathbf{J}_i
$$

where $j_{\parallel,i}$ is the parallel ion current density, $\mathbf{J}_i$
is the ion current-density vector, and
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the
local magnetic-field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

This quantity applies locally at a plasma-facing surface, including a
divertor surface; it is not surface- or flux-surface-averaged. Contributions
from all included ion species and charge states are summed algebraically.
Each charge-state contribution equals its [parallel ion charge-state
particle flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux) multiplied by
its electric charge. Electron current is excluded.

It is the ion contribution to [current density](name:current_density)
projected along the magnetic field, whereas [parallel current
density](name:parallel_current_density) has no ion-only restriction. It is
neither the magnitude of the ion current-density vector nor its projection
onto the surface normal.

Sign convention: Positive when net conventional ion charge transport is in
the direction of the local magnetic-field vector.

items.name: ion_torque_density_due_to_thermalization
items.description:
Angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume delivered to a thermal plasma
population when fast or nonthermal particles undergo thermalization.
items.documentation:
Torque density due to thermalization is the signed rate at which angular
momentum is transferred per unit volume from a fast or otherwise nonthermal
population to the thermal plasma population as particles become assimilated
into the thermal background. It represents a momentum source for the thermal
population, rather than an energy-transfer rate.

For a resolved angular-momentum component $a$, the defining relation is

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{th}}^{(a)} = \left.\frac{\partial \ell_{\mathrm{th}}^{(a)}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{thermalization}}
$$

where $\tau_{\mathrm{th}}^{(a)}$ is the thermalization-attributed torque
density and $\ell_{\mathrm{th}}^{(a)}$ is the angular-momentum density of
the thermal population in component $a$.

The quantity includes only momentum transfer attributed to thermalization
and is not the total torque from all momentum-transfer mechanisms. The
[thermal-ion torque density due to
thermalization](name:thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_thermalization) is a
species-resolved instance of this general quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when thermalization increases the angular-momentum
density of the thermal population in the resolved component.

items.name: accumulated_total_gas_count
items.description:
Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of all gas species delivered by
injection after plasma breakdown, summed across species.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of gas
introduced into the plasma by injection after plasma breakdown. It combines
all injected gas species into one total inventory.

The total is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t) = \sum_s z_s N_s(t)
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t)$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron count, $s$
identifies an injected gas species, $N_s(t)$ is the cumulative number of
particles of species $s$ delivered since plasma breakdown, and $z_s$ is the
equivalent-electron contribution per particle; for an atomic species, $z_s$
is its atomic number, while for a molecule it is the sum of the atomic
numbers of its constituent atoms.

The quantity applies to all gas species and uses a cumulative sum over the
post-breakdown injection history. It excludes gas introduced during prefill
before plasma breakdown, instantaneous injection rates, and any
single-species inventory such as [accumulated hydrogen count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection).

It is the post-breakdown counterpart of the prefill inventory [accumulated
total prefill gas count](name:accumulated_total_prefill_gas_count); the two
quantities differ by the injection phase they accumulate.

items.name: perpendicular_runaway_electron_particle_flux
items.description:
Cross-field number flux of runaway electrons through magnetic flux surfaces,
obtained by projecting their particle-flux vector onto the outward
flux-surface normal.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the cross-field component of runaway-electron particle
transport through magnetic flux surfaces. It describes the directed rate at
which the suprathermal runaway-electron population crosses those surfaces,
rather than transport along magnetic field lines.

The component is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{RE},\perp}=\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{\mathrm{RE}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}_{\mathrm{FS}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the [runaway electron particle
flux](name:runaway_electron_particle_flux) vector and $\hat{\mathbf
n}_{\mathrm{FS}}$ is the unit normal to the magnetic flux surface, directed
toward increasing flux label. The subscript $\perp$ denotes the cross-field
projection.

This is a signed normal component, not the magnitude of the full
particle-flux vector and not a field-aligned flux. It is distinct from
cross-field transport coefficients such as [perpendicular runaway electron
diffusivity](name:perpendicular_runaway_electron_diffusivity) and from
[perpendicular runaway electron convection
velocity](name:perpendicular_runaway_electron_convection_velocity).

Sign convention: Positive when runaway-electron particle transport is
directed toward increasing flux label, outward from the magnetic axis.

items.name: total_thermal_ion_pressure
items.description:
Total pressure of thermal ions is the isotropic kinetic stress from random
motion, summed over all ion species and ionic charge states, excluding fast
ions and bulk-flow stress.
items.documentation:
Total pressure of thermal ions is the isotropic part of the kinetic pressure
tensor arising from random motion of all thermal-ion populations. It
combines their thermal stresses rather than selecting one ion species, one
charge state, or one directional pressure component.

The total is defined by summing the centered thermal pressure moments:

$$
p_{i,\mathrm{tot}}^{\mathrm{th}} = \sum_s p_s^{\mathrm{th}} = \frac{1}{3}\sum_s\sum_c m_s\int |\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{s,c}|^2 f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{i,\mathrm{tot}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the total thermal-ion pressure,
$s$ labels ion species, $p_s^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the [thermal ion
pressure](name:thermal_ion_pressure) of species $s$ summed over its ionic
charge states, $c$ labels ionic charge states, $m_s$ is the species mass,
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{s,c}$ is the mean velocity
of the corresponding thermal population, $f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is its
velocity distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume
element.

The aggregation is a direct additive sum over all ion species and ionic
charge states, not a density-weighted mean. It excludes electron pressure,
neutral pressure, fast-ion pressure, and bulk-flow kinetic stress. The word
“total” denotes species aggregation within the thermal-ion population, not
inclusion of nonthermal ions.

Each [thermal ion charge-state
pressure](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_pressure) contributes to its species
pressure and hence to this total. Adding the thermal electron pressure gives
the [thermal plasma pressure](name:thermal_plasma_pressure).

items.name: radial_neutral_velocity
items.description:
Major-radius component of a neutral species' mean flow in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, with number-density-weighted averaging over
contributing internal states.
items.documentation:
The radial neutral velocity is the major-radius projection of the bulk flow
of a selected neutral species. It describes directed motion after averaging
over particle velocities. The direction is defined in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal
symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

At a given position, the component is defined by

$$
u_{0R}=\hat{R}\cdot\mathbf{u}_0=\frac{\sum_a n_{0,a}\,\hat{R}\cdot\mathbf{u}_{0,a}}{\sum_a n_{0,a}}
$$

where $u_{0R}$ is the radial neutral velocity, $\hat{R}$ is the unit vector
toward increasing major radius, and $\mathbf{u}_0$ is the [neutral
velocity](name:neutral_velocity) vector. The index $a$ labels the
contributing neutral internal states, $n_{0,a}$ is their individual number
density, and $\mathbf{u}_{0,a}$ is their individual mean particle velocity.

The quantity applies to one neutral species and excludes charged particles.
When multiple internal states contribute, their velocities are combined as a
number-density-weighted mean, not summed; [bulk neutral internal-state
velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity) instead retains a
single state's flow. The mean requires nonzero total neutral density.

This is a signed directional component, not the flow magnitude, a particle
flux, or an effective momentum-convection coefficient. The major-radius
direction is not generally normal to a magnetic flux surface. The [vertical
neutral velocity](name:vertical_neutral_velocity) is the vertical projection
of the same mean-flow vector.

Sign convention: Positive when the neutral bulk flow has a component toward
increasing major radius, away from the toroidal symmetry axis.

items.name: accumulated_neon_count
items.description:
Cumulative number of neon atoms from gas injection accumulated since plasma
breakdown, expressed in equivalent electrons; each injected neon atom
contributes ten equivalent electrons.
items.documentation:
Cumulative number of neon atoms from gas injection accumulated since plasma
breakdown is the time integral of the neon atom injection rate due to gas
injection, weighted by the neon atomic number. It is a species-specific
accumulated count expressed in equivalent electrons, so each injected neon
atom contributes $Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}=10$ equivalent electrons.

The accumulated neon count $N_{\mathrm{Ne,acc}}$ is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{Ne,acc}}(t) = Z_{\mathrm{Ne}} \int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ne,inj}}(t') \, dt'
$$

where $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time, $t$ is the evaluation
time, $t'$ is the integration time, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ne,inj}}$ is the
neutral-neon atom injection rate due to gas injection, and
$Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}=10$ is the number of electrons in a neutral neon atom.

The scope is neon supplied by gas injection during the interval from plasma
breakdown to the evaluation time; the aggregation is cumulative over
injected neon atoms, with equivalent-electron weighting applied per atom. It
excludes neon present before breakdown, neon supplied by non-gas-injection
sources, retained inventory, pumped-out amount, and charge-state-resolved
plasma neon populations.

This quantity is the accumulated gas-injection counterpart of the species
neon count convention, with the additional accumulation interval and
equivalent-electron weighting. It follows the same accumulated
equivalent-electron convention as [accumulated krypton
count](name:accumulated_krypton_count) and [accumulated ammonia
count](name:accumulated_ammonia_count); a neutral-neon atom count without
equivalent-electron weighting is obtained by dividing by $Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}$.

items.name: wave_phase_of_antenna_strap
items.description:
Phase angle of the radio-frequency current phasor carried by one
ion-cyclotron-heating antenna strap, defined relative to a specified RF
phase reference.
items.documentation:
Wave phase of an antenna strap is the phase angle of the oscillatory
radio-frequency current phasor carried by that strap. It describes the
strap-level excitation phase used in the antenna's toroidal phasing
configuration.

The complex strap-current phasor may be represented as

$$
I_s = |I_s|e^{i\phi_s}
$$

where $I_s$ is the complex radio-frequency current phasor, $|I_s|$ is its
current amplitude, and $\phi_s$ is the wave phase represented by this
quantity. The phase is defined modulo $2\pi$ relative to a specified RF
reference phase.

This quantity applies to one antenna strap and is not summed or averaged
over multiple straps. It refers to the phase of the strap current, not the
phase of a forward power-wave phasor, which is represented by [forward wave
phase of an ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna](name:forward_wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), or the
phase associated with a complete antenna element.

The associated [wave current of antenna
strap](name:wave_current_of_antenna_strap) provides the phasor whose phase
is specified, while wave current of antenna strap amplitude determines its
magnitude rather than its phase. Relative phases between straps determine
the toroidal phasing of the antenna excitation and therefore influence the
launched wave excitation spectrum. The phase-reference plane and any
phase-unwrapping convention must be specified separately when comparing
values.

items.name: toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential_imaginary_part
items.description:
Imaginary quadrature of the complex toroidal magnetic-vector-potential
perturbation eigenfunction for a linear MHD mode in the plasma.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the imaginary quadrature of the first-order perturbed
magnetic vector potential eigenfunction for a specified linear MHD mode in
the plasma. It is projected onto the toroidal direction of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

The defining relation is

$$
\delta A_{\phi}^{\mathrm{im}}(\mathbf{x}) = \operatorname{Im}\!\left[\delta A_{\phi}(\mathbf{x})\right]
$$

where $\delta A_{\phi}^{\mathrm{im}}$ is the imaginary component,
$\operatorname{Im}$ extracts the imaginary part, $\delta A_{\phi}$ is the
complex toroidal component of the perturbed magnetic vector potential, and
$\mathbf{x}$ is the position in the plasma. Here, $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity applies only to the perturbed plasma eigenfunction and excludes
equilibrium or unperturbed magnetic-vector-potential contributions. It is
the imaginary quadrature, not the full complex component and not the
toroidal component of the perturbed magnetic field. Its sign and magnitude
depend on the phase convention selected for the complex eigenfunction.

This quantity is the imaginary-part transformation of the [toroidal
perturbed plasma magnetic vector
potential](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential);
together with the corresponding real quadrature, it reconstructs the complex
toroidal component. It is distinct from the [toroidal perturbed plasma
magnetic field imaginary
part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part), which
represents a magnetic-field component rather than a vector-potential
component.

items.name: incident_soft_xray_radiance
items.description:
Incident soft X-ray power radiance gives received electromagnetic power per
projected detector area and solid angle, integrated over the selected energy
band.
items.documentation:
Incident soft-X-ray power radiance is the energy-integrated radiant power
arriving at a receiving surface from the viewing direction, expressed per
projected area and per solid angle.

$$
L_{\rm inc} = \int_{\mathcal{E}} L_E^{\rm inc}\,dE = \frac{dP_{\rm inc}}{dA_\perp\,d\Omega}
$$

where $L_{\rm inc}$ is the incident power radiance, $L_E^{\rm inc}$ is the
incident spectral power radiance at photon energy $E$, $\mathcal{E}$ is the
selected photon-energy band or collection of bands, $P_{\rm inc}$ is
incident radiant power, $A_\perp$ is projected receiving area, and $\Omega$
is accepted solid angle.

The quantity applies to soft X-ray radiation incident on a detector channel,
with spectral dependence integrated over the selected energy band or bands.
It is an incoming radiometric quantity per area and solid angle, not a total
power integrated over the detector aperture or viewing directions, and it is
distinct from detector-registration efficiency.

Integrating this radiance over the relevant projected area and solid angle
gives the band-integrated received power represented by [power of soft X-ray
detector](name:power_of_soft_xray_detector). Unlike [hard X-ray
brightness](name:hard_xray_brightness), which is photon-number radiance,
this quantity is power radiance; [spectral efficiency of soft X-ray
detector](name:spectral_efficiency_of_soft_xray_detector) instead describes
the probability that incident photons are registered.

items.name: poloidal_angle_of_plasma_boundary_gap
items.description:
Poloidal angle of a plasma-boundary gap specifies its measurement direction,
measured clockwise from the outward horizontal direction in the poloidal
cross-section.
items.documentation:
Poloidal angle of plasma boundary gap

For a nonzero directed segment aligned with the measurement direction, the
defining relation is:

$$\theta = \operatorname{atan2}(Z_{\mathrm{axis}} - Z,\; R - R_{\mathrm{axis}})$$

where $\theta$ is the gap-measurement direction angle, $(R_0, Z_0)$ and
$(R_1, Z_1)$ are the segment's start and end coordinates, and
$\operatorname{atan2}$ is the two-argument inverse tangent. The right-handed
cylindrical frame is $(R, \phi, Z)$, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The angle applies separately to each plasma-boundary gap, not to an average
over the boundary. It describes a direction rather than the positional
poloidal angle of the gap's reference point about the magnetic axis. Zero
corresponds to the outward horizontal direction, and angles differing by a
full turn describe the same direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the measurement direction rotates clockwise
from increasing $R$ toward decreasing $Z$, viewed with $R$ to the right and
$Z$ upward.

items.name: toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force
items.description:
Flux-surface-averaged toroidal angular-momentum source per unit volume from
the magnetic force on counter-passing particles' current across magnetic
flux surfaces.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the flux-surface-averaged toroidal angular-momentum source
density delivered to counter-passing particles by the magnetic Lorentz force
associated with their current across magnetic flux surfaces. Toroidal
angular momentum is angular momentum about the symmetry axis; its source is
a [torque density](name:torque_density), not a toroidal force density.

The defining relation is

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{ctr}} = \left\langle R\,\left(j_{n,\mathrm{ctr}}\hat{\mathbf n}\times\mathbf B\right)\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol\phi}\right\rangle_\psi
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{ctr}}$ is this torque density,
$j_{n,\mathrm{ctr}}$ is the signed conventional current density carried
across magnetic flux surfaces by counter-passing particles, $\hat{\mathbf
n}$ is the unit normal toward increasing flux-surface label $\psi$, and
$\mathbf B$ is the magnetic field. The brackets denote a normalized average
over the surface labeled by $\psi$. In the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is the distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is
the toroidal angle, $Z$ is the vertical coordinate, and
$\hat{\boldsymbol\phi}$ points toward increasing $\phi$. The moment arm $R$
remains inside the average.

Counter-passing particles occupy nontrapped passing orbits whose circulation
along the magnetic field opposes the plasma-current direction. Only the
counter-passing part of the specified particle species' distribution
contributes; co-passing and trapped particles and other torque mechanisms
are excluded. This is a flux-surface average, not an unaveraged local source
or a volume-integrated torque.

This quantity is the toroidal angular-momentum source component of the
[counter-passing Lorentz-force torque
density](name:counter_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force). The
[co-passing
counterpart](name:toroidal_co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force)
applies the same mechanism to co-passing particles. It is distinct from the
[thermal-plasma return-current
torque](name:toroidal_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force), which acts on
thermal plasma through compensating currents.

Sign convention: Positive when the magnetic force supplies toroidal angular
momentum in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: trapped_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Trapped collisional torque density is the vector rate of angular-momentum
transfer per plasma volume to a specified thermal ion charge state from
Coulomb collisions with trapped particles.
items.documentation:
Trapped collisional torque density is the vector rate of angular-momentum
transfer per unit plasma volume to thermal ions of a specified charge state
from Coulomb collisions with the trapped population.

With $\mathrm{tr}$ denoting the trapped population and $z$ denoting the
selected thermal ion charge state, the torque-density vector is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll},z}^{\mathrm{tr}} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll},z}^{\mathrm{tr}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll},z}^{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the trapped
collisional torque-density vector delivered to charge state $z$,
$\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the angular-momentum origin to the
local plasma point, and $\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll},z}^{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the
collisional force density transferred to that charge state by Coulomb
collisions with trapped particles.

This quantity is charge-state resolved and orbit-class resolved: it applies
to the selected thermal ion charge state and includes only the
trapped-population contribution to the collisional angular-momentum source.
It excludes co-passing- and counter-passing-population contributions, torque
densities summed over charge states, noncollisional momentum sources, and
the collisional force density before multiplication by the lever arm.

The sum of the trapped, [co-passing collisional torque
density](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions),
and [counter-passing collisional torque
density](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
contributions gives the corresponding orbit-class-summed [collisional torque
density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions) for
the same thermal ion charge state when these populations form the orbit
partition.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component of the torque-density
vector is aligned with the positive orientation of the corresponding basis
direction or angular-momentum axis; for toroidal angular momentum in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, positive is in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: electron_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer
items.description:
Characteristic outward distance over which electron number density decreases
by one e-folding in the scrape-off layer.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the e-folding distance for electron number density that
decreases outward from the confined plasma into the open-field-line
scrape-off layer. It is the electron-density member of the [decay-length
family](name:decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer), distinct from the ion
decay length.

$$
L_e = \left|\frac{d\ln n_e}{dx}\right|^{-1}
$$

where $L_e$ is the electron-density e-folding length, $n_e$ is electron
number density, and $x$ is outward distance normal to magnetic flux
surfaces. The quantity is defined locally where the logarithmic gradient is
nonzero; the magnitude gives the positive distance associated with the
outward decrease. It does not denote the decay length of temperature or heat
flux, which are separate members of the family.

items.name: energy_velocity_due_to_convection
items.description:
Effective advection velocity characterizing transport of plasma energy by
bulk convection, without restricting the transported energy to a particular
species or ion charge state.
items.documentation:
Energy convective velocity is the effective advection velocity associated
with non-diffusive transport of plasma energy by bulk convection. It is the
energy-channel instance of [velocity due to
convection](name:velocity_due_to_convection), without resolving a particular
species or ion charge state.

The convective energy-flux density is related to the transported energy
density by

$$
\Gamma_{E,\mathrm{conv}} = w_E v_{E,\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{E,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective energy-flux density,
$w_E$ is the transported energy density, and $v_{E,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the
effective advection velocity in the represented transport direction.

The quantity excludes diffusive, conductive, and source contributions.
Charge-state-resolved energy transport is represented by [ion charge-state
energy velocity due to
convection](name:ion_charge_state_energy_velocity_due_to_convection), while
the electron-specific formulation is [electron energy convection
velocity](name:electron_energy_convection_velocity).

items.name: volume_averaged_ion_temperature
items.description:
Temperature of a specified ion species from random kinetic motion,
arithmetically averaged over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed
magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Temperature of a specified ion species averaged over the plasma volume
enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface describes its random
translational kinetic energy. It excludes kinetic energy associated with
directed mean ion flow.

The volume average of the local [ion temperature](name:ion_temperature) is
defined by

$$
\langle T_i\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V T_i\,dV
$$

where $\langle T_i\rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged temperature of the
specified ion species, $T_i$ is its local temperature, $V$ is the plasma
volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface, and $dV$ is the
differential physical-volume element.

For the specified species, the local temperature is the density-weighted
mean over all charge states, rather than a sum of charge-state temperatures;
[ion charge-state temperature](name:ion_charge_state_temperature) resolves
an individual charge state. The subsequent spatial average weights local
temperature by physical volume, not by particle number. It is neither a
local temperature nor a volume-integrated thermal energy, and it does not
combine different ion species.

Unlike [ion average temperature](name:ion_average_temperature), which
combines ion species and charge states by number-density weighting, this
quantity retains the selected species. Its sibling, [volume-averaged total
ion temperature](name:volume_averaged_total_ion_temperature), instead
volume-averages the effective temperature of the combined thermal-ion
population. This species-specific volume average also supplies the
denominator of the [axis-to-volume-average ion-temperature
ratio](name:ratio_of_ion_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_ion_temperature),
which expresses central temperature peaking.

items.name: toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of nitrogen ions, evaluated on
the last closed magnetic flux surface at the plasma boundary.
items.documentation:
The toroidal nitrogen-ion bulk-flow velocity is the density-weighted mean
directed motion of all nitrogen ion charge states along the geometric
toroidal direction at the plasma boundary, which is the last closed magnetic
flux surface.

The charge-state-averaged velocity is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{N}} = \frac{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{N},z} v_{\phi,\mathrm{N},z}}{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{N},z}}
$$

where $z$ is the nitrogen ion charge-state index, $n_{\mathrm{N},z}$ is the
number density of that charge state, and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{N},z}$ is its
toroidal bulk-flow velocity. Neutral nitrogen is excluded. The corresponding
[toroidal oxygen velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) has the same
definition with oxygen replacing nitrogen, while [toroidal nitrogen velocity
at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) uses
a different evaluation locus.

items.name: ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Effective Fickian coefficient for particle transport by ions in a specified
charge state, relating diffusive flux to that charge state’s density
gradient without selecting a spatial direction.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective Fickian particle diffusion coefficient for
ions in a specified charge state. It describes transport of that
charge-state population without summing over ion charge states or selecting
a spatial projection.

The diffusive particle flux is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{i,q}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{i,q}\nabla n_{i,q}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{i,q}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive particle
flux of ion charge state $q$, $D_{i,q}$ is this diffusion coefficient, and
$n_{i,q}$ is the number density of that charge state.

The [radial ion charge-state diffusion
coefficient](name:radial_ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) and
[poloidal ion charge-state diffusion
coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) are
directional forms of this quantity. The charge-state-specific scope
distinguishes it from the [electron diffusion
coefficient](name:electron_diffusion_coefficient), which describes electron
particle transport.

items.name: radial_coordinate_at_outboard_midplane
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate of a magnetic flux surface at the outboard midplane,
locating the surface's low-field-side point relative to the toroidal
symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
Major-radius coordinate at outboard midplane

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the major-radius
coordinate is related to the horizontal Cartesian coordinates by:

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}
$$

where $R$ is the [major-radius coordinate](name:radial_coordinate) measured
as perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is the
toroidal angle increasing counterclockwise when viewed from above
$+\hat{Z}$, $Z$ is vertical height, and $x$ and $y$ are the horizontal
Cartesian coordinates of the evaluated point in the right-handed Cartesian
$(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$ and origin on the
toroidal symmetry axis.

The quantity applies separately to each magnetic flux surface, identified by
its poloidal magnetic-flux label $\psi$, where $\psi$ denotes the flux
function labeling nested magnetic surfaces. It is a point value evaluated at
the outboard midplane of the specified surface; it is not a flux-surface
average and excludes the inboard intersection.

For an up-down-symmetric equilibrium, the outboard midplane of every flux
surface lies at the vertical height of the magnetic axis, so this quantity
coincides with the major radius of the surface's low-field-side intersection
with the horizontal plane through the magnetic axis. For a
non-up-down-symmetric equilibrium, the outboard midplane of a surface lies
at a different height, and the low-field-side intersection taken at the
magnetic-axis height does not coincide with this quantity.

It is a locus-specific specialization of the general [major-radius
coordinate](name:radial_coordinate), evaluated at the outboard midplane. The
corresponding [radial coordinate at the inboard
midplane](name:radial_coordinate_at_inboard_midplane) locates the distinct
high-field-side intersection of the same type of magnetic surface.

The low-field-side equatorial midplane: the point of maximum major radius on
the flux surface in question. For a value at the separatrix intersection use
outboard_midplane_separatrix. Where $R = \max_{S} R,\quad R >
R_{\mathrm{axis}}$, $S$ is the magnetic flux surface the point lies on;
$R_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is major radius of the magnetic axis.

items.name: ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Fick's-law proportionality coefficient relating the density-normalized
diffusive thermal energy flux of a specified ion charge state to its local
temperature gradient, serving as the direction-agnostic parent over its
radial and poloidal component forms.
items.documentation:
The ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient $D_{i,z,E}$ quantifies
gradient-driven diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by ions in a
specified charge state $z$, providing the Fick's-law proportionality between
the density-normalized diffusive ion heat flux for that charge state and the
local ion temperature gradient for the same charge state. It is the
charge-state-resolved specialization of the [ion energy diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) and is distinct from
convective, advective, or $E \times B$ contributions to the total ion heat
flux.

The defining relation for the density-normalized diffusive energy flux of
charge state $z$ is:

$$
\frac{\mathbf{Q}_{i,z,\mathrm{diff}}}{n_{i,z}} = -D_{i,z,E}\,\nabla T_{i,z}
$$

where $\mathbf{Q}_{i,z,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive thermal-energy flux
carried by ions in charge state $z$, $n_{i,z}$ is their number density, and
$T_{i,z}$ is their [temperature](name:ion_charge_state_temperature). The
minus sign denotes transport down the local temperature gradient.

This quantity applies to one specified ion charge state and is not an
aggregation over charge states. The corresponding charge-state-aggregated
[ion energy diffusion coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) is
a density-weighted mean over all ion species and charge states. Directional
children include radial_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient, for
the component associated with $\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$
is vertical height, and
poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient, for the poloidal
component.

items.name: perturbed_plasma_velocity
items.description:
Complex vector eigenfunction of the first-order bulk plasma velocity
perturbation in linear MHD stability analysis, encoding the spatial
amplitude and phase of oscillatory plasma flow for a specified toroidal
Fourier mode.
items.documentation:
In linear MHD stability theory, the perturbed plasma velocity is the complex
vector eigenfunction $\delta\hat{\mathbf{v}}(\mathbf{r})$ representing the
spatial structure of the first-order oscillatory perturbation of the bulk
plasma flow about a magnetohydrostatic equilibrium — the linearized
counterpart to the equilibrium [plasma_velocity](name:plasma_velocity). The
eigenfunction encodes both the spatial amplitude and the relative phase of
the velocity oscillation as a function of position in the plasma.

The full space-time perturbation field is assembled as:

$$
\delta\mathbf{v}(\mathbf{r},t) = \delta\hat{\mathbf{v}}(\mathbf{r})\,e^{i(n\phi - \omega t)}
$$

where $n$ is the toroidal mode number, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, and $\omega$ is the complex
mode frequency whose real part gives the oscillation frequency and imaginary
part gives the growth or damping rate. In ideal MHD the eigenfunction
satisfies $\delta\hat{\mathbf{v}} = -i\omega\boldsymbol{\xi}$, where
$\boldsymbol{\xi}$ is the plasma displacement vector.

The eigenfunction decomposes into three spatial projections:
[radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity),
[toroidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity),
and
[poloidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity),
all complex-valued. The overall amplitude and phase are
normalization-dependent unless anchored to a physical constraint such as
kinetic energy. The growth rate of the associated mode is characterized by
[per_toroidal_mode_growth_rate](name:per_toroidal_mode_growth_rate) and the
spatial phase reference by mode_phase; companion scalar perturbed
eigenfunctions include
[perturbed_plasma_temperature_real_part](name:perturbed_plasma_temperature_real_part)
and
[perturbed_plasma_pressure_imaginary_part](name:perturbed_plasma_pressure_imaginary_part).

items.name: electron_emissivity
items.description:
Local electromagnetic radiation power emitted by the electron population per
unit volume, without specifying a particular radiation mechanism.
items.documentation:
Electron emissivity is the local electromagnetic radiation power emitted by
the electron population per unit volume. It represents an emission source
attributable to electrons, not the net energy change of the electron
population.

At position $\mathbf{x}$, the emissivity is defined by

$$
\varepsilon_e(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{dP_e^{\mathrm{rad}}}{dV}
$$

where $\varepsilon_e$ is electron emissivity, $P_e^{\mathrm{rad}}$ is the
radiation power emitted by electrons, $V$ is volume, and $\mathbf{x}$ is
position.

A particular radiation mechanism may be selected by the surrounding physical
context, but no mechanism is implied by this name. The quantity excludes
absorbed power and differs from [power density due to
radiation](name:power_density_due_to_radiation), which is not
electron-specific, and from electron power density, which denotes net energy
transfer in the electron energy balance.

items.name: neutral_gas_pressure_of_gauge
items.description:
Neutral gas pressure of a gage is the pressure indicated by a barometry gage
for residual neutral gas in the vacuum vessel or surrounding vacuum system.
It represents local vacuum conditions rather than a kinetic neutral-particle
pressure moment.
items.documentation:
Neutral gas pressure of a gage is the local residual-neutral-gas pressure
indicated by a barometry gage. The word gage identifies the instrument
producing the indication and does not mean a pressure difference relative to
atmosphere.

The quantity applies to neutral gas contributing to the gage response in the
vacuum vessel or surrounding vacuum system. It aggregates the gage response
without resolving thermal, fast, species, or internal-state components.

This instrument-indicated quantity is distinct from kinetic neutral-particle
pressures such as [total neutral pressure](name:total_neutral_pressure),
[thermal neutral pressure](name:thermal_neutral_pressure), [neutral
internal-state pressure](name:neutral_internal_state_pressure), and [total
neutral internal-state
pressure](name:total_neutral_internal_state_pressure). Those quantities
denote pressure moments or state-resolved sums of neutral particle
populations, whereas neutral gas pressure of a gage denotes the pressure
represented by the barometry gage response and need not equal any one
kinetic component.

items.name: magnetic_shear_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Magnetic shear at the plasma boundary is the logarithmic derivative of the
safety factor with respect to the outward normalized toroidal flux radius.
items.documentation:
Magnetic shear at plasma boundary

The defining relation is

$$
\hat{s} = \frac{\rho}{q}\frac{dq}{d\rho}
$$

where $\hat{s}$ is the magnetic shear, $q$ is the safety factor, and $\rho$
is the normalized toroidal flux radius, increasing outward. The expression
is evaluated at the plasma boundary, using the limit from the
confined-plasma side when required and where that limit exists.

The scope is a single boundary evaluation, with no additional flux-surface
averaging or averaging over neighboring flux surfaces. It is not an integral
across the edge or the magnetic shear evaluated at another named locus.

This quantity is the plasma-boundary specialization of [magnetic shear at a
flux surface](name:magnetic_shear_at_flux_surface): it uses the same
logarithmic safety-factor derivative, with the evaluation locus fixed to the
plasma boundary.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

items.name: electron_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Signed local volumetric rate of Coulomb-collisional energy exchange for a
designated electron population, positive for net energy gain.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the net local volumetric energy exchange caused by Coulomb
collisions for a designated electron target population. It represents energy
deposited in or removed from that target, excluding noncollisional
energy-transfer mechanisms.

The collisional power density is defined by

$$
P_a^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_b Q_{a\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $P_a^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the net collisional power density for
electron target population $a$, $Q_{a\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the
Coulomb-collisional energy-transfer rate from partner population $b$ to
target $a$, and the superscript $\mathrm{coll}$ denotes the
Coulomb-collisional contribution.

The target $a$ is an electron population, and the sum over $b$ includes the
collision partners and subpopulations established by the quantity's
aggregation scope. This is an electron-target contribution rather than an
unrestricted sum of collisional energy exchange for all plasma populations;
noncollisional transfer mechanisms are excluded.

It is the electron-target specialization of [power density due to
collisions](name:power_density_due_to_collisions). The accepted [thermal
electron collisional power
density](name:thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions) is a more
specific instance with the bulk thermal electron population as target and
fast particle populations as partners, whereas [thermal ion collisional
power
density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) has
an ion target and is not included in this electron quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when the designated electron target population
gains energy from its collision partners.

items.name: toroidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part
items.description:
Toroidal perturbed plasma velocity real part is the real part of the complex
amplitude of the toroidal component of the first-order plasma velocity
perturbation for a single toroidal Fourier harmonic with mode number n in
the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It is the in-phase
eigenfunction component relative to the chosen complex phase, not the
equilibrium toroidal flow.
items.documentation:
Toroidal perturbed plasma velocity real part is the real part of the complex
amplitude of the toroidal component of the first-order plasma velocity
perturbation for a single toroidal Fourier harmonic with mode number $n$.
The toroidal component is the projection along $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$,
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is
vertical height. It represents the in-phase part of the linear
magnetohydrodynamic perturbation eigenfunction relative to the chosen
complex phase, not the equilibrium toroidal flow.

The component is defined by projecting the complex velocity eigenfunction
for the selected harmonic onto the toroidal basis direction and taking the
real part:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Re},n}(R,Z) = \operatorname{Re}\!\left[\widetilde{\mathbf v}_n(R,Z)\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}\right]
$$

where $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Re},n}$ is this quantity, $\widetilde{\mathbf v}_n$
is the complex first-order plasma velocity eigenfunction for toroidal mode
number $n$, $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector, and
$\operatorname{Re}$ denotes the real part. With toroidal dependence
proportional to $\exp(i n\phi)$, $i$ is the imaginary unit.

Together with [toroidal perturbed plasma velocity imaginary
part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_imaginary_part), this quantity
forms the complex toroidal perturbed velocity amplitude. Because a linear
eigenfunction may be multiplied by an arbitrary complex constant, the
division into real and imaginary parts depends on the selected normalization
and phase; the quadrature component is the linked imaginary part, not a
separate physical velocity direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the real toroidal velocity component points
in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: poloidal_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Dimensionless coefficient scaling the free-streaming bound on poloidal
neutral momentum flux, limiting its magnitude without reversing its
direction.
items.documentation:
The poloidal neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient sets the
free-streaming bound on the poloidal component of neutral-particle
[momentum](name:momentum) transport in a fluid closure. It constrains the
modeled flux magnitude rather than specifying a momentum source or a
diffusivity.

The limiting bound is expressed as:

$$
\left|\Pi_{0,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{lim}}\right| \leq \Pi_{0,\mathrm{p}}^{\max} = \alpha_{0,\mathrm{p}}\Pi_{0,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\Pi_{0,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limited poloidal neutral
momentum-flux component, $\Pi_{0,\mathrm{p}}^{\max}$ is its allowed
magnitude, $\alpha_{0,\mathrm{p}}$ is this nonnegative coefficient, and
$\Pi_{0,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the nonnegative free-streaming
reference magnitude defined by the closure. The subscript $0$ denotes
neutrals and $\mathrm{p}$ denotes the poloidal component. Limiting preserves
the direction of the unrestricted flux; this coefficient does not prescribe
a particular interpolation formula.

This is the poloidal directional component of the [neutral momentum
flux-limiter coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
not a magnitude combining all directional components. It applies to the
neutral population represented by the closure, excluding ion momentum
transport. Unlike the [poloidal neutral-state momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
it is not resolved for an individual neutral internal state; no summation or
averaging rule for state-specific coefficients is implied.

items.name: per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_power_density
items.description:
Absorbed coherent-wave power density deposited in thermal ions of a selected
species, resolved by toroidal mode number and represented locally across a
poloidal cross-section or as a flux-surface average.
items.documentation:
Absorbed coherent-wave power density per toroidal mode is the rate at which
energy from one toroidal Fourier component of a coherent wave is transferred
directly to the thermal ions of a selected species per unit physical volume.
It describes either the local spatial distribution across a poloidal
cross-section or the flux-surface average of that density.

For the local quantity, the mode-resolved deposition density is

$$
p_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{(n_\phi)}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{dP_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{(n_\phi)}}{dV}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $p_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the absorbed power density,
$P_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the power transferred to the selected
species' thermal ions by the coherent-wave harmonic with toroidal mode
number $n_\phi$, $V$ is physical volume, and $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial
position. The index $i$ identifies the selected ion species, and
$\mathrm{th}$ identifies its thermal population.

The quantity applies to the thermal-ion population of one selected species
and one toroidal mode, and is summed over all charge states of that species,
not over distinct ion species or modes. It may retain local variation across
a poloidal cross-section or be averaged over a magnetic flux surface; the
flux-surface average is not a pointwise value.

It excludes absorption by electrons and nonthermal ions, as well as energy
transfer through non-wave processes; it is not the net thermal-ion energy
source from all processes. The [charge-state-resolved
counterpart](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density)
resolves contributions by ion charge state, while [fast-ion power density
per toroidal mode](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_power_density) describes
deposition into nonthermal ions.

Summing the modal contributions gives the mode-summed [thermal-ion absorbed
wave power density](name:thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power_density) for the
same species and spatial averaging convention. Integrating the local density
over the plasma volume gives the [thermal-ion absorbed wave power per
toroidal mode](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power),
which is a power rather than a power density.

Sign convention: Positive when coherent-wave energy is transferred to the
thermal ions of the selected species.

items.name: line_averaged_lithium_density
items.description:
Path-length-averaged total number density of lithium ions along a specified
plasma chord, summed over Li+ through fully stripped Li3+ and excluding
neutral lithium.
items.documentation:
This is the path-length average of lithium ion number density, summed over
all ionization stages from Li$^+$ through fully stripped Li$^{3+}$, along a
specified chord through the plasma.

The chord average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{Li} \rangle_L = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_{Li}(s)\,ds
$$

where $n_{Li}(s)$ is the local lithium ion number density in m$^{-3}$, $s$
is path length in meters along the chord, and $L$ is the total chord length
in meters.

This quantity weights each path-length element equally and excludes neutral
lithium. It differs from the flux-surface-averaged lithium density at the
plasma boundary, which averages over a separatrix, and from [volume-averaged
lithium density](name:volume_averaged_lithium_density), which averages over
confined plasma volume.

items.name: accumulated_nitrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description:
Cumulative post-breakdown nitrogen inventory delivered by gas injection,
expressed as seven equivalent-electron counts for each injected nitrogen
atom.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of nitrogen
delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown. It represents the
nitrogen contribution to the injected fueling and impurity inventory.

The equivalent-electron inventory is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}} = Z_{\mathrm{N}} N_{\mathrm{N}}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the cumulative equivalent-electron inventory,
$Z_{\mathrm{N}}=7$ is the atomic number of nitrogen, and $N_{\mathrm{N}}$ is
the cumulative number of nitrogen atoms delivered by gas injection after
breakdown.

The quantity applies only to nitrogen delivered after plasma breakdown and
aggregates all such delivered nitrogen over the accumulation interval. It is
a cumulative inventory, not an instantaneous injection rate, and it is the
nitrogen-specific contribution rather than an all-species inventory.

The equivalent-electron convention counts seven contributions per nitrogen
atom; it does not represent the number of free electrons currently present
in the plasma and is independent of the nitrogen ionization state. This
convention is shared by accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection, which
applies the corresponding atomic-number weighting to accumulated carbon.

items.name: toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Density-weighted toroidal flow velocity of xenon ions at the radial location
assigned to the internal transport barrier, averaged over all xenon
ionization states.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local xenon-ion bulk-flow velocity projected onto the
toroidal direction at the flux-surface radius assigned to the internal
transport barrier. It is averaged over xenon ionic charge states; neutral
xenon is excluded.

$$
