v_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe}}=\frac{\sum_q n_q\left(\mathbf{v}_q\cdot\hat{\phi}\right)}{\sum_q n_q}
$$

where $q$ indexes xenon ionization states, $n_q$ is the number density of
state $q$, $\mathbf{v}_q$ is its bulk velocity in m s$^{-1}$, and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $R$ the major radius, $\phi$ the toroidal angle,
and $Z$ the vertical height. The corresponding xenon-ion quantities at the
[magnetic axis](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) and [pedestal
top](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_pedestal_top) use the same aggregation
and projection at different radial locations.

Sign convention: Positive when the xenon-ion flow has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: parallel_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective velocity coefficient for advective, non-diffusive transport of
total momentum in the field-parallel direction, distinct from the total
momentum bulk flow velocity.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective coefficient describing the advective,
non-diffusive transport of total momentum in the field-parallel direction.
It is a transport closure quantity, not the actual bulk flow velocity
associated with total momentum.

For the parallel momentum component, the convective momentum flux is defined
by

$$
\Gamma_{P,\parallel,\mathrm{conv}} = V_{\mathrm{conv},\parallel} P_\parallel
$$

where $\Gamma_{P,\parallel,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective flux of
parallel momentum, $V_{\mathrm{conv},\parallel}$ is the parallel component
of momentum convection velocity, and $P_\parallel$ is the parallel momentum
density.

The parallel component is directed along the local magnetic-field direction.
The quantity applies to the total momentum equation without restricting the
momentum to ions, neutrals, a species, or a charge state; it therefore
differs in population scope from [parallel neutral particle convection
velocity](name:parallel_neutral_particle_convection_velocity) and in
direction from [vertical momentum convection
velocity](name:vertical_momentum_convection_velocity).

items.name: resistance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
items.description:
Resistance of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the real part of the
effective radio-frequency loading impedance at the antenna feed reference
plane. It represents the resistive component associated with power coupled
to the plasma and dissipative antenna losses.
items.documentation:
Resistance of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the real part of the
effective radio-frequency loading impedance presented by the antenna at its
feed reference plane. It characterizes the component of the antenna load
that absorbs radio-frequency power, including plasma loading and intrinsic
dissipative losses, distinct from the reactive energy storage represented by
antenna capacitance or inductance.

The antenna loading impedance is decomposed into resistive and reactive
parts as:

$$
Z_\mathrm{ant} = R_\mathrm{ant} + i X_\mathrm{ant}
$$

where $Z_\mathrm{ant}$ is the complex antenna loading impedance,
$R_\mathrm{ant}$ is the antenna resistance in ohms, $X_\mathrm{ant}$ is the
antenna reactance in ohms, and $i^2=-1$.

For a sinusoidal strap current, the resistive power associated with this
load is $P_\mathrm{res}=R_\mathrm{ant} I_\mathrm{rms}^2$, where
$P_\mathrm{res}$ is in watts and $I_\mathrm{rms}$ is the root-mean-square
wave current of the antenna strap in amperes. This quantity is a feed-plane
impedance component and is not itself a forward, reflected, or net power;
those powers describe traveling-wave energy flow in the connected
radio-frequency circuit.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient_over_edge_region
items.description:
Vector flux-limiter coefficient that sets an edge-region, nonnegative
componentwise cap on neutral-particle momentum-flux density for a specified
internal state as a fraction of its collisionless free-streaming bound,
without reversing any flux component.
items.documentation:
Vector flux-limiter coefficient that applies to neutral particles occupying
a specified internal state over the edge region is the set of directional
coefficients used to bound components of the corresponding neutral
internal-state momentum-flux density. The internal state may be an
electronic, vibrational, rotational, or other resolved excitation state, and
the coefficient applies separately to each physical direction used to
decompose the momentum-flux vector.

For directional component $k$, the limiter defines the admissible cap:

$$
|\Pi_{\mathrm{lim},k}| \le \lambda_k\,|\Pi_{\mathrm{fs},k}|,\qquad 0 \le \lambda_k \le 1
$$

where $\Pi_{\mathrm{lim},k}$ is the limited directional component of the
neutral internal-state momentum flux over the edge region,
$\Pi_{\mathrm{fs},k}$ is the corresponding collisionless free-streaming
component whose magnitude defines the bound, $\lambda_k$ is this coefficient
component, and $k$ indexes a physical direction rather than the internal
state. If a component is specified in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame, with basis $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, then $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counterclockwise when
viewed from $+\hat{Z}$, $Z$ is vertical height, and $k$ may identify an
$\hat{R}$, $\hat{\phi}$, or $\hat{Z}$ projection; field-aligned components
use their explicitly named local directions, such as parallel to the
magnetic field.

The inequality is a cap on magnitude rather than an equality for the
realized momentum flux. Because $\lambda_k$ is nonnegative, applying the
limiter may reduce or bound a signed momentum-flux component but does not
reverse its direction; a nonzero limited component retains the sign of the
underlying component to which the cap is applied. This coefficient is not
the momentum-flux vector itself and is distinct from limiters for particle
flux or energy flux.

items.name: ion_rotation_frequency
items.description:
Angular-velocity vector of an ion species’ bulk rotational motion,
density-weighted over all ionic charge states and distinct from gyrocenter
orbit motion.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the bulk rotational angular-velocity vector of an ion
species, aggregated over its ionic charge states. It describes collective
ion motion rather than the orbital angular velocity of individual
gyrocenters.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\Omega}_i = \frac{\sum_Z n_{i,Z}\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{i,Z}}{\sum_Z n_{i,Z}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Omega}_i$ is the species bulk rotation-frequency vector,
$n_{i,Z}$ is the number density of species $i$ in charge state $Z$, and
$\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{i,Z}$ is the rotation-frequency vector of that charge
state, represented by [ion charge state rotation
frequency](name:ion_charge_state_rotation_frequency). The toroidal
projection is represented by [toroidal ion rotation
frequency](name:toroidal_ion_rotation_frequency).

The quantity includes only bulk rotational motion and is not a gyrocenter
orbit-frequency diagnostic or a charge-state-resolved value.

Sign convention: Positive when a component of $\boldsymbol{\Omega}_i$ points
along the corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical
$(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ basis.

items.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_source
items.description:
Momentum source density for a specified ion charge state gives the net
directed momentum transfer into that state, retaining the full vector before
directional projection.
items.documentation:
The momentum source density for a specified ion charge state is the net
directed rate of momentum transfer into that state, represented by a
physical vector before projection onto a coordinate or magnetic-field
direction. It is the charge-state-resolved member of the [momentum source
density](name:momentum_source), whereas
[ion_momentum_source](name:ion_momentum_source) aggregates the corresponding
ion contributions over charge states.

$$
\mathbf{S}_{m,s} = \frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbf{P}_s}{\mathrm{d}A\,\mathrm{d}t}
$$

where $\mathbf{P}_s$ is the net momentum transferred to ion charge state
$s$, $A$ is the reference area, and $t$ is time.

The state index $s$ identifies one resolved ion charge state; contributions
are not summed over charge states. Positive and negative terms represent net
momentum addition and removal. Directional forms, such as the [toroidal ion
charge-state momentum
source](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source), are projections of
this vector. It differs from
[ion_charge_state_momentum_flux](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux), which
describes momentum transported across a surface rather than locally
transferred into the state.

Sign convention: Positive when a vector component points along its stated
positive direction: increasing $R$, $\phi$, or $Z$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, or along the defined positive local
magnetic-field direction for a parallel component.

items.name: inner_radius_of_poloidal_field_coil
items.description:
Bore-side radius of one poloidal-field-coil element's annular conductor
cross-section, measured from the common center of its circular boundaries.
items.documentation:
The inner radius is the smaller of the two radii bounding the annular
conductor cross-section of one poloidal-field-coil element. It extends from
the common annulus center to the inner conducting boundary in a poloidal
plane.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the inner
radius $R_{\mathrm{in}}$ is defined by

$$
R_{\mathrm{in}} = \sqrt{(R_b-R_c)^2 + (Z_b-Z_c)^2}
$$

where $R_b$ and $Z_b$ are the coordinates of any point on the inner circular
boundary, and $R_c$ and $Z_c$ are the coordinates of the annulus center, all
evaluated at the same toroidal angle.

Together with the [outer radius](name:outer_radius_of_poloidal_field_coil)
and their common center, this radius specifies the annular cross-section of
the individual element, not the combined geometry of all coil elements. The
radii satisfy $0 \le R_{\mathrm{in}} < R_{\mathrm{out}}$, where
$R_{\mathrm{out}}$ is the outer boundary radius. The inner radius is
distinct from the major-radius coordinate of the annulus center. It equals
the [circular-arc contour radius](name:radius_of_poloidal_field_coil) for an
arc lying on this inner circular boundary.

items.name: propane_prefill_count
items.description:
Propane prefill count is the total amount of C3H8 introduced before plasma
breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 26 count units per
neutral propane molecule.
items.documentation:
Propane prefill count is the total amount of neutral propane (C3H8)
introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count. Each propane molecule contributes 26 equivalent
electrons: 18 from three carbon atoms and 8 from eight hydrogen atoms.

The equivalent-electron count is obtained by accumulating the injected
propane molecules over the prefill interval:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{C_3H_8,prefill}} = (3Z_C + 8Z_H)N_{\mathrm{C_3H_8,prefill}} = 26N_{\mathrm{C_3H_8,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_\mathrm{bd}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{C_3H_8,prefill}}$ is the
equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{C_3H_8,prefill}}$ is the accumulated
propane molecule count, $Z_C=6$ and $Z_H=1$ are the atomic numbers of carbon
and hydrogen, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}$ is the propane molecule injection
rate, $t_0$ is the start of prefill, and $t_\mathrm{bd}$ is the
plasma-breakdown time.

This quantity includes only propane introduced before breakdown and excludes
later fueling, other gas species, and the retained or ionized inventory. It
uses the common equivalent-electron bookkeeping of
[prefill_count](name:prefill_count), with
[ethane_prefill_count](name:ethane_prefill_count) providing the analogous
molecular-species convention.

items.name: poloidal_conductivity
items.description:
Local electrical response coefficient relating a poloidal electric field to
conductive current density along the flux-surface tangent in a
constant-toroidal-angle plane.
items.documentation:
Poloidal conductivity is the poloidal-poloidal projection of the local
electrical-conductivity tensor. The poloidal direction is tangent to a
magnetic flux surface within a plane of constant toroidal angle, rather than
normal to the surface.

The defining projection is:

$$
\sigma_{\mathrm{pp}} = \hat{e}_{\mathrm{p}} \cdot \boldsymbol{\sigma} \cdot \hat{e}_{\mathrm{p}}
$$

where $\sigma_{\mathrm{pp}}$ is poloidal conductivity, $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$
is the electrical-conductivity tensor, and $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the
geometric poloidal unit tangent. The geometry is specified in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For an electric field directed entirely along the poloidal tangent, the
conductive response satisfies
$j_{\mathrm{c,p}}=\sigma_{\mathrm{pp}}E_{\mathrm{p}}$, where
$j_{\mathrm{c,p}}$ is the induced poloidal conductive current density and
$E_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal electric-field component. This is a local
plasma response coefficient, not a flux-surface average or an integrated
conductance. It does not include off-diagonal coupling from electric-field
components in other directions. Reversing the poloidal unit tangent leaves
the coefficient unchanged.

Unlike [parallel conductivity](name:parallel_conductivity), this coefficient
projects onto a geometric poloidal tangent rather than the magnetic-field
direction. [Toroidal conductivity](name:toroidal_conductivity) is the
corresponding toroidal-toroidal projection of the same
electrical-conductivity tensor.

items.name: incident_neutron_power_of_breeder_blanket_module
items.description:
Total power carried by fusion neutrons onto a single breeder blanket module
before nuclear energy is deposited in its materials.
items.documentation:
Incident neutron power is the incoming fusion-neutron energy rate delivered
to one breeder blanket module. It represents the module-level neutron load
at the boundary before interactions convert neutron energy into deposited
heat.

The power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{n,inc}} = \frac{dE_{\mathrm{n,inc}}}{dt}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{n,inc}}$ is the total incident neutron power,
$E_{\mathrm{n,inc}}$ is the cumulative energy carried by neutrons incident
on the module, and $t$ is time.

This quantity applies to a single breeder blanket module and is aggregated
over the module's complete incident neutron load. It is a total incoming
power, not a local surface power density or a power assigned to an
individual material layer. It excludes energy deposited within the module by
neutron interactions, which is represented by [nuclear heating power of a
breeder blanket
module](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket_module), and it is
distinct from incident photon power represented by [incident radiated power
of a breeder blanket
module](name:incident_radiated_power_of_breeder_blanket_module).

Incident neutron power is an input to the module energy budget and provides
the neutron-power basis for the [tritium breeding ratio of a breeder blanket
module](name:tritium_breeding_ratio_of_breeder_blanket_module). It is
therefore distinct from the broader [power of a breeder blanket
module](name:power_of_breeder_blanket_module), which encompasses multiple
incident, deposited, and transferred power components.

items.name: toroidal_volumetric_force
items.description:
Toroidal component of the electromagnetic body-force density vector acting
on plasma volumes or conducting wall and structural elements, projected onto
increasing toroidal angle φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The toroidal volumetric force is the $\hat{\phi}$-projection of the local
electromagnetic body-force density vector acting on plasma volumes or
conducting wall and structural elements. It characterizes the local
mechanical load per unit volume directed around the torus in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For the magnetic Lorentz body force, the toroidal projection is:

$$
f_\phi = \mathbf{f}\cdot\hat{\phi} = (\mathbf{J}\times\mathbf{B})\cdot\hat{\phi} = J_Z B_R - J_R B_Z
$$

where $f_\phi$ is the toroidal volumetric force, $\mathbf{f}$ is the
electromagnetic body-force density vector, $\mathbf{J}$ is current density,
$\mathbf{B}$ is magnetic field, and $J_R$, $J_Z$, $B_R$, and $B_Z$ are the
corresponding projections in the same right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame. The magnetic-field vector entering this relation is the quantity
represented by [magnetic field](name:magnetic_field).

This quantity is one signed projection of [volumetric
force](name:volumetric_force), complementary to [radial volumetric
force](name:radial_volumetric_force) and [vertical volumetric
force](name:vertical_volumetric_force). It excludes the magnitude of the
body-force density vector and any force integrated over a finite volume.

Sign convention: Positive when the force density points in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame.

items.name: temperature_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Temperature at the divertor target is the energy-equivalent temperature of a
specified plasma population evaluated at the plasma side of a
divertor-target sheath. It refers to the sheath-entrance plasma population,
not to the solid target material or to an average over different
populations.
items.documentation:
Temperature at the divertor target is the energy-equivalent temperature of a
specified plasma population evaluated at the plasma side of a
divertor-target sheath. It characterizes the random kinetic part of the
particle distribution at the sheath entrance, the boundary at which
sheath-entry conditions such as the Bohm criterion are posed, and is not a
thermodynamic property of the solid target material.

For a population $s$, the scalar target temperature is the one-third trace
of the kinetic thermal-energy moment over the velocity-space domain of that
population at the sheath entrance:

$$
T_{s,t} = \frac{m_s}{3 n_{s,t}} \int_{\mathcal{V}_{s,t}} |\mathbf{v} - \mathbf{u}_{s,t}|^2 f_{s,t}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $T_{s,t}$ is the temperature at the divertor target for population
$s$, subscript $t$ denotes the divertor-target sheath entrance, $m_s$ is the
particle mass of population $s$, $n_{s,t}$ is the number density of that
population at the sheath entrance, $\mathcal{V}_{s,t}$ is the full
velocity-space domain of the specified sheath-entrance population,
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{s,t}$ is the mean flow
velocity of the population at the sheath entrance, $f_{s,t}$ is its velocity
distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The
distribution normalization is such that integrating $f_{s,t}$ over
$\mathcal{V}_{s,t}$ gives $n_{s,t}$.

The specified population can be an electron population, an ion population, a
charge state, or another plasma population identified separately. If a
species is represented without charge-state resolution, this intensive value
is the density-weighted mean over all charge states. The unqualified
quantity does not imply an average over different plasma populations or over
positions on the divertor target.

For the electron population it corresponds to the [electron temperature at
divertor target](name:electron_temperature_at_divertor_target), and for the
ion population it corresponds to the [ion temperature at divertor
target](name:ion_temperature_at_divertor_target). It is the divertor-target
specialization of the more general [plasma
temperature](name:plasma_temperature). The moment definition makes it two
thirds of the population-averaged random kinetic energy at the sheath
entrance, not the full mean random kinetic energy per particle.

items.name: thickness_of_optical_element
items.description:
Thickness of an optical element defined by the separation between its front
and back surfaces along the element-local normal axis.
items.documentation:
Thickness of optical element

The thickness is defined by

$$
d = \left\|\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{back}}-\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{front}}\right\|
$$

where $d$ is the thickness, and $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{front}}$ and
$\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{back}}$ are the position vectors of the front- and
back-surface intersections with the same line parallel to the element-local
normal axis.

The quantity describes one element, not a combined thickness of multiple
elements. It is distinct from the geometric path length of an obliquely
propagating ray and from optical path length, which includes
refractive-index weighting.

The [first local tangential
width](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_optical_element) and [second
local tangential
width](name:second_local_tangential_width_of_optical_element) describe the
element's complementary tangential extents rather than its front-to-back
separation.

items.name: total_thermal_ion_energy
items.description:
Volume-integrated internal energy of the complete thermal-ion ensemble,
obtained from its total isotropic pressure and excluding fast or
suprathermal ions.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the internal energy stored in the random thermal motion of
all confined thermal ions, summed over every ion species and charge state.
It is the complete-population specialization of thermal_ion_energy.

Its defining relation is

$$
U_i = \frac{3}{2}\int_{V_{\rm pl}} p_i(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $U_i$ is the total thermal-ion energy, $p_i(\mathbf{r})$ is the total
isotropic thermal-ion pressure, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $dV$ is the volume
element, and $V_{\rm pl}$ is the confined plasma volume. The pressure is
summed over all thermal ion species and charge states, consistent with
[total_thermal_ion_pressure](name:total_thermal_ion_pressure). Fast,
suprathermal, and other nonthermal ion populations are excluded.

items.name: y_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector
items.description:
Cartesian y component of the unit vector aligned with the unshattered pellet
velocity direction immediately before shattering.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the projection onto the Cartesian y axis of the
unit-normalized direction of the unshattered pellet velocity immediately
before shattering.

The component is defined by

$$
u_y = \hat{\mathbf{u}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{y}}, \qquad \hat{\mathbf{u}} = \frac{\mathbf{v}}{|\mathbf{v}|}
$$

where $u_y$ is the y component, $\hat{\mathbf{u}}$ is the pellet
injection-direction unit vector, $\mathbf{v}$ is the unshattered pellet
velocity, $|\mathbf{v}|$ is its magnitude, and $\hat{\mathbf{y}}$ is the y
unit vector in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$
frame.

This quantity describes direction only, not pellet speed or position. Its
value is bounded between $-1$ and $1$; together with the [x component of the
pellet-injector unit vector](name:x_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector) and [z
component of the pellet-injector direction unit
vector](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector), it specifies the
injection direction.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe
items.description:
Vertical position of the geometric center of a toroidal magnetic-field probe
coil, expressed as the signed Z coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical
(R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The vertical coordinate identifies the geometric center of an individual
toroidal magnetic-field probe coil in the right-handed cylindrical basis
$(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$, with coordinates $(R,\phi,Z)$. It locates
the coil and does not represent the magnetic field sensed by the probe.

The coordinate is the projection of the center position onto the vertical
basis direction:

$$
Z_{\mathrm{probe}} = \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{center}} \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{probe}}$ is the probe-center vertical coordinate,
$\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{center}}$ is the position vector from the
cylindrical-frame origin to the geometric center of the coil, and $\hat{Z}$
is the vertical unit vector. Here $R$ denotes major radius, $\phi$ denotes
toroidal angle, and $Z$ denotes vertical coordinate.

The quantity applies to one toroidal magnetic-field probe coil center. It is
not summed, averaged, or weighted over windings, probes, or a spatial
region. It excludes the probe's sensitive-axis orientation and the local
magnetic-field value, and is distinct from the corresponding position
coordinate for a [poloidal magnetic-field
probe](name:vertical_coordinate_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe).

As the $Z$ component of the coil-center position, this coordinate
complements the radial and toroidal position coordinates in locating the
probe within the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

Sign convention: Positive when the probe-coil center lies in the $+Z$
direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: poloidal_gyrocenter_frequency
items.description:
Poloidal component of gyrocenter orbit angular frequency, equal to the
signed rate of gyrocenter advance in poloidal angle θ within flux
coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
items.documentation:
The poloidal gyrocenter frequency is the poloidal component of gyrocenter
orbit angular frequency in the flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$,
where $\rho$ is a radial flux-surface label, $\theta$ is poloidal angle, and
$\phi$ is toroidal angle. It describes gyrocenter advance after averaging
over the fast cyclotron gyration, retaining the slower drift and bounce or
transit motion.

It is defined by

$$
\omega_{\theta,gc} = \frac{d\theta_{gc}}{dt}
$$

where $\omega_{\theta,gc}$ is the poloidal gyrocenter angular frequency,
$\theta_{gc}$ is the gyrocenter poloidal angle measured in radians, and $t$
is time measured in seconds.

This component is distinct from the [toroidal gyrocenter
frequency](name:toroidal_gyrocenter_frequency), which measures advance in
$\phi$; together they form the [gyrocenter
frequency](name:gyrocenter_frequency). Passing particles can circulate
continuously in poloidal angle, whereas trapped particles reverse their
poloidal motion during bounce excursions. The fast cyclotron angular
frequency is excluded.

Sign convention: Positive when the gyrocenter advances in the direction of
increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

items.name: ion_torque_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Collisional torque on the ion population is the net angular-momentum
transfer produced by interactions with other particle populations.
items.documentation:
Collisional torque on the ion population is the net angular-momentum
transfer produced by collisional forces acting on ions.

For a volume-integrated torque component about a selected axis, the defining
relation is

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{coll},a}^{\mathrm{ion}} = \int_V \left(\mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{ion}}\right)_a\,dV
$$

where $\tau_{\mathrm{coll},a}^{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the torque transferred to
ions, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector relative to the selected rotation
axis, $\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the collisional force
density acting on ions, $V$ is the plasma volume, and $a$ identifies the
reported torque direction.

This quantity is the ion-population specialization of [torque due to
collisions](name:torque_due_to_collisions); [thermal ion torque due to
collisions](name:thermal_ion_torque_due_to_collisions) is a more specific
instance restricted to thermal ions. It represents momentum exchange with
collision partners and excludes noncollisional torque sources.

Sign convention: Positive when collisional momentum exchange transfers
angular momentum to the ion population in the positive sense of the selected
axis; for the toroidal direction, positive means increasing $\phi$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: toroidal_coordinate_at_beam_tracing_point
items.description:
Azimuthal location of a beam-tracing point around the machine symmetry axis,
expressed by the toroidal angle in the right-handed (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The toroidal coordinate $\phi$ identifies the azimuthal location of a
beam-tracing point about the machine symmetry axis. It is the angular
coordinate of that geometric point, rather than a beam direction or a field
value sampled at the point.

The coordinate is defined from the point's horizontal Cartesian position by:

$$
\phi = \operatorname{atan2}(Y,X)
$$

where $X$ and $Y$ are the horizontal position coordinates in the
right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis, with
$\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$
is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height; the $\phi=0$ reference follows
the facility coordinate convention. This is the beam-tracing-point instance
of the general [toroidal coordinate](name:toroidal_coordinate).

Sign convention: Positive when the point lies in the direction of increasing
toroidal angle $\phi$, counter-clockwise when viewed from above along
$+\hat{Z}$.

items.name: ethane_prefill_count
items.description:
Ethane prefill count is the total amount of neutral ethane (C2H6) introduced
before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 18
equivalent electrons per molecule.
items.documentation:
Ethane prefill count is the total amount of neutral ethane (C2H6) introduced
during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count. Each neutral ethane molecule contributes 18
equivalent electrons: 12 from its two carbon atoms and 6 from its six
hydrogen atoms.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{C_2H_6,prefill}} = 18N_{\mathrm{C_2H_6,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}18\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{C_2H_6,prefill}}$ and
$N_{\mathrm{C_2H_6,prefill}}$ are pure counts, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}$
is the neutral-ethane introduction rate in molecules s$^{-1}$, and $t_0$,
$t_{\mathrm{bd}}$, and $t$ are the prefill start, plasma-breakdown, and time
variables in seconds.

This quantity includes only neutral ethane introduced before breakdown and
excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas
injection, and retained or ionized inventory. It is the ethane component of
[prefill_count](name:prefill_count);
[accumulated_ethane_count](name:accumulated_ethane_count) represents
distinct post-breakdown accumulation, while
[ethylene_prefill_count](name:ethylene_prefill_count) applies the same
convention to a different hydrocarbon.

items.name: length_of_pellet
items.description:
End-to-end extent of an intact cylindrical pellet measured along its
symmetry axis before injection or shattering.
items.documentation:
The pellet axial length is the distance between the two end faces measured
parallel to the symmetry axis of the intact cylindrical pellet.

$$
L_p = z_2 - z_1
$$

where $L_p$ is the axial length and $z_1$ and $z_2$ are the axial
coordinates of the two end faces, ordered so that $z_2 > z_1$ along the
chosen axial direction.

This quantity describes the unshattered pellet before injection or
fragmentation and excludes its transverse size, which is described by the
[diameter of the pellet](name:diameter_of_pellet).

items.name: toroidal_argon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of argon ions at the magnetic
axis, combining all ionization states in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ,
Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The toroidal argon velocity at the magnetic axis is the local bulk-flow
component of argon ions projected onto the toroidal unit vector in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It combines Ar+
through Ar18+ and excludes neutral argon; the magnetic axis is where the
gradient of poloidal magnetic flux $\psi$ vanishes.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}}(R_{\mathrm{axis}},Z_{\mathrm{axis}})=\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{k+}}v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{k+}}}{\sum_{k=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{k+}}}
$$

where $V_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}}$ and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{k+}}$ are toroidal
velocities in m.s$^{-1}$, $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{k+}}$ is the local number density
in m$^{-3}$, and $(R_{\mathrm{axis}},Z_{\mathrm{axis}})$ are the
magnetic-axis coordinates in m. The denominator corresponds to the
charge-state-summed [argon density at the magnetic
axis](name:argon_density_at_magnetic_axis); the species and locus semantics
parallel [toroidal nitrogen velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).

Sign convention: Positive when the charge-state-averaged argon-ion bulk flow
points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, along
$+\hat{\phi}$.

items.name: poloidal_magnetic_field
items.description:
Poloidal magnetic field is the strength of local magnetic induction in the
plane containing the toroidal symmetry axis and the evaluation point,
excluding the toroidal contribution.
items.documentation:
Poloidal magnetic field is the magnitude of the projection of the local
[magnetic induction](name:magnetic_field) onto the poloidal plane. It
retains the radial and vertical contributions while excluding the toroidal
contribution.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, it is defined
by:

$$
B_{\mathrm{p}} = \sqrt{B_R^2 + B_Z^2}
$$

where $B_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal magnetic-field strength, $B_R$ is the
cylindrical radial magnetic-field component, and $B_Z$ is the vertical
magnetic-field component.

This is a local quantity without a prescribed evaluation locus, spatial
averaging, or restriction to a particular field source. It is neither the
full magnetic-field magnitude nor the signed sensing-axis projection
associated with the [poloidal magnetic field of a magnetic-field
probe](name:poloidal_magnetic_field_of_magnetic_field_probe).

The [poloidal magnetic field at the pedestal
top](name:poloidal_magnetic_field_at_pedestal_top) specializes this quantity
by fixing its evaluation locus.

items.name: ion_charge_state_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
items.description:
Outgoing recombination energy flux at the wall is the emitted energy per
unit area and time attributable to a specified incident-ion species and
charge state.
items.documentation:
Ion charge-state energy flux at the wall due to recombination is the
outgoing energy transfer associated with surface recombination of a
specified incident-ion species and charge state. The charge-state label
identifies the incident ion responsible for recombination, not the charge
state of an emitted product.

The local emitted energy flux is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{W,s,Z}^{\mathrm{em,rec}} = \frac{\partial^2 W_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{em,rec}}}{\partial A\,\partial t}
$$

where $\Gamma_{W,s,Z}^{\mathrm{em,rec}}$ is the outgoing recombination
energy flux attributable to incident-ion species $s$ and charge state $Z$,
$W_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{em,rec}}$ is the corresponding cumulative emitted
recombination-associated energy, $A$ is wall area, and $t$ is time. The
superscripts $\mathrm{em}$ and $\mathrm{rec}$ denote emission and
recombination, respectively.

The quantity applies locally at the wall, with incident-ion species and
charge state held fixed. Recombination channels and emitted product species
and states are summed; incident-ion species and charge states are not. It is
an energy flux per unit area, not a wall-integrated power, and excludes
energy transferred through non-recombination channels.

Summing over incident-ion species and charge states gives the [ion energy
flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination), the
ion-associated contribution to the broader [energy flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination). Unlike the
[incident-ion recombination energy
flux](name:incident_ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination), this
quantity describes energy emitted from the wall rather than energy delivered
to it. It is neither incoming kinetic-energy flux nor an
incident-minus-emitted net balance.

items.name: voltage_of_poloidal_field_coil
items.description:
Signed terminal voltage across a poloidal-field-coil winding, equal to its
resistive voltage drop plus the voltage induced by changing magnetic flux
linkage.
items.documentation:
The terminal voltage is the total voltage drop across a poloidal-field-coil
winding. It combines the ohmic voltage drop in the conductor with the
inductive voltage associated with changing magnetic flux linkage.

Using a consistent winding orientation, the voltage is defined by

$$
V_{\mathrm{term}} = R_{\mathrm{w}} I + \frac{d\Phi_{\mathrm{link}}}{dt}
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{term}}$ is the terminal voltage, $R_{\mathrm{w}}$ is the
winding resistance represented by the [poloidal-field-coil
resistance](name:resistance_of_poloidal_field_coil), $I$ is the conventional
current in the winding, $\Phi_{\mathrm{link}}$ is its signed total magnetic
flux linkage, and $t$ is time.

This quantity applies to the complete active winding and includes both
self-field and externally produced flux linkage. It is distinct from the
induced terminal voltage of a separate [poloidal magnetic-field
probe](name:voltage_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe) and is analogous to
the [toroidal-field-coil terminal
voltage](name:voltage_of_toroidal_field_coil).

Sign convention: Positive when the terminal potential drop is measured in
the direction of the winding's defined positive conventional-current
direction.

items.name: height_of_passive_structure
items.description:
Full vertical extent of a rectangular cross-section of a passive conducting
structure element, measured parallel to Z in the right-handed cylindrical
(R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The height is the full vertical extent of a rectangular cross-section of a
passive conducting structure element, measured along the vertical direction
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

It is defined by the difference between the upper and lower vertical
coordinates:

$$
H = Z_{\max} - Z_{\min}
$$

where $H$ is the full height, and $Z_{\max}$ and $Z_{\min}$ are the vertical
coordinates of the upper and lower cross-section boundaries, respectively.

This quantity is the full height, not a half-height, local thickness, or
horizontal width. Its corresponding horizontal dimension is the [full
horizontal width of a passive conducting structure
element](name:width_of_passive_structure).

items.name: volume_of_pellet_fragment
items.description:
Geometric volume occupied by the material of an individual shattered pellet
fragment, distinguishing fragment size from the intact pellet and
surrounding propellant.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the geometric volume enclosed by the material boundary of
one shattered pellet fragment. It describes the fragment’s physical size
rather than the volume of the complete pellet, injector, or surrounding
propellant.

The volume is defined from the fragment’s material domain:

$$
V_f = \int_{\mathcal{D}_f} d^3\mathbf{r}
$$

where $V_f$ is the volume of the individual fragment, $\mathcal{D}_f$ is the
three-dimensional region occupied by its material, and $d^3\mathbf{r}$ is
the volume element integrated over that region.

The scope is one individual fragment within the shattered-pellet population.
This is an extensive geometric quantity for that fragment and is not an
aggregate over multiple fragments; it excludes surrounding gas and does not
represent the volume of the intact pellet, injector, or complete fragment
cloud.

The associated [toroidal coordinate of the pellet
fragment](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_pellet_fragment) locates the same
fragment around the machine symmetry axis, while this quantity characterizes
its geometric size.

items.name: vertical_outline_of_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Signed vertical height of each point on the plasma-boundary outline in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, defining its poloidal
cross-sectional shape.
items.documentation:
The vertical outline coordinate is the signed height of each point on the
plasma-boundary contour in a poloidal cross-section. It describes the
boundary geometry rather than a field, flux, or scalar boundary summary.

The coordinate is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height. Each outline point has its own $Z$ value; the quantity is
neither an average nor an extremum over the boundary.

This quantity applies specifically to the plasma-boundary outline and
excludes the outline of a plasma-facing component. Together with the
corresponding [radial outline of the plasma
boundary](name:radial_outline_of_plasma_boundary), it specifies the boundary
contour in the poloidal $(R,Z)$ plane. The analogous vertical coordinate for
a component boundary is [vertical outline of the plasma-facing
component](name:vertical_outline_of_plasma_facing_component).

Sign convention: Positive when the point lies in the direction of increasing
vertical coordinate $Z$.

items.name: lower_inner_squareness_of_flux_surface
items.description:
Dimensionless Luce (2013) squareness coefficient for the lower-inner,
high-field-side quadrant of a nested magnetic flux surface, measuring signed
departure from a reference ellipse.
items.documentation:
The lower-inner squareness of a flux surface is the dimensionless Luce
(2013) shape coefficient that characterizes how the lower, high-field-side
quadrant of a nested toroidal magnetic flux surface departs from a reference
ellipse sharing the same center, horizontal half-width, and
[elongation](name:elongation_of_flux_surface). It is the lower-quadrant
component of [inner squareness of a flux
surface](name:inner_squareness_of_flux_surface), complementary to
[upper-inner squareness of a flux
surface](name:upper_inner_squareness_of_flux_surface).

The reference ellipse is parameterized in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame by

$$
\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{ref}}(\theta)=\left(R_0+a\cos\theta,\;Z_0+\kappa a\sin\theta\right)
$$

where $R$ is major radius, $Z$ is vertical height, $\theta$ is a poloidal
parameter, $(R_0,Z_0)$ is the ellipse center, $a$ is its horizontal
half-width, and $\kappa$ is its elongation. Within the Luce model,
$\zeta_{\mathrm{li}}=0$ represents no additional lower-inner corner shaping;
positive values indicate an outward, boxier corner and negative values an
inward, more indented corner.

This coefficient describes only the lower high-field-side quadrant and is
not an average of the upper and lower inner coefficients.

items.name: tungsten_density_at_limiter
items.description:
Local particle number density of tungsten ions evaluated in the boundary
plasma immediately adjacent to the plasma-facing limiter surface, summed
over ionization states and excluding neutral tungsten.
items.documentation:
Number density of tungsten ions evaluated at the plasma-limiter interface on
the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance. The limiter
terminates open magnetic field lines in the scrape-off layer, so this
quantity describes the tungsten impurity population participating in
limiter-adjacent plasma–surface interactions.

The charge-state sum is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm W} = \sum_{Z\ge 1} n_{\mathrm{W}^{Z+}} = \sum_{Z\ge 1}\int f_{\mathrm{W}^{Z+}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm W}$ is the total tungsten-ion number density, $Z$ is the
positive tungsten charge number, $n_{\mathrm{W}^{Z+}}$ is the density of
charge state $Z$, and $f_{\mathrm{W}^{Z+}}(\mathbf{v})$ is its velocity
distribution function. The sum includes all tungsten ionization states and
excludes neutral tungsten.

This quantity specializes [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter) to
tungsten and contributes to ion_density_at_limiter. It is evaluated at the
limiter rather than the divertor-target location used by
[tungsten_density_at_divertor_target](name:tungsten_density_at_divertor_target).

items.name: toroidal_torque_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Local rate of angular-momentum transfer about the plasma symmetry axis per
unit volume attributable to pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic dynamics.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the diamagnetic contribution to the local source of angular
momentum about the plasma symmetry axis. It describes the torque per unit
volume associated with the toroidal momentum source, rather than the
toroidal projection of a torque vector.

Its relation to the toroidal force density is

$$
\tau_{\phi}^{\mathrm{dia}} = R f_{\phi}^{\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic toroidal torque
density and $f_{\phi}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic contribution to the
toroidal force density in the momentum balance. In the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is distance from the symmetry axis,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical position.

The quantity includes only the contribution attributed to
pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic dynamics, not the full torque density
from all mechanisms. It applies to the population included in the momentum
balance; no particular species or all-species sum is implied. Population
contributions add when an aggregate torque density is formed.

Unlike [momentum flux due to diamagnetic
drift](name:momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), which describes
linear-momentum transfer across an oriented surface, this quantity is a
volume source of angular momentum. A nonzero local contribution does not by
itself establish a nonzero net torque integrated over the plasma.

Sign convention: Positive when the diamagnetic momentum source acts in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: parallel_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Dimensionless factor setting the collisionless free-streaming upper bound on
field-aligned ion momentum flux without reversing the flux direction.
items.documentation:
The parallel ion momentum flux limiter coefficient sets the collisionless
free-streaming cap for gradient-driven transport of ion
[momentum](name:momentum) along the local magnetic field. Limiting restricts
the flux magnitude without reversing its direction.

The coefficient defines the cap through:

$$
\Pi_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{cap}} = \alpha_{i,\parallel}\Pi_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\alpha_{i,\parallel}$ is this coefficient,
$\Pi_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{cap}}$ is the nonnegative upper bound on the
field-aligned ion momentum-flux magnitude, and
$\Pi_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the corresponding collisionless
free-streaming reference magnitude. The subscript $i$ identifies the
selected ion population, and $\parallel$ denotes the local magnetic-field
direction. The limited flux magnitude cannot exceed this cap; the
coefficient does not prescribe a particular interpolation between the
unlimited flux and the cap.

This is the field-aligned component of the [ion momentum flux limiter
coefficient](name:ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), whereas the
[poloidal ion momentum flux limiter
coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) selects
the poloidal component. It applies to ion rather than neutral momentum
transport and is a limiter parameter, not a momentum flux or diffusivity. No
sum or average over ion species or charge states is implied.

items.name: current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity
items.description:
Vector electric current density arising from heat-viscosity terms in the
collisional plasma fluid closure, where the divergence of the heat-viscosity
stress tensor drives net charge transport in a magnetized plasma.
items.documentation:
The heat-viscosity current density is the electric current density vector
generated when heat-viscosity contributions in a collisional plasma fluid
model (such as the Braginskii closure) induce net species motion that
results in charge transport. In a magnetized plasma, the viscous stress
tensor $\overset{\leftrightarrow}{\pi}$ contains a heat-viscosity part
$\overset{\leftrightarrow}{\pi}_\mathrm{hv}$ that couples heat transport to
bulk plasma momentum; the divergence of this tensor enters the fluid
momentum equation for each species and drives flows carrying net electric
current.

The heat-viscosity current density vector $\mathbf{j}_\mathrm{hv}$ is
expressed as:

$$
\mathbf{j}_\mathrm{hv} = \sum_s q_s n_s \mathbf{v}_{s,\mathrm{hv}}
$$

where $q_s$ is the charge of species $s$, $n_s$ is its number density, and
$\mathbf{v}_{s,\mathrm{hv}}$ is the flow velocity component driven by
heat-viscosity forces in the species momentum balance.

This vector is decomposed into geometric projections, including the [radial
component](name:radial_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity) along
$\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The
companion quantity current_density_due_to_collisions captures the distinct
inter-species collisional friction mechanism, while
radial_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity represents the analogous
contribution from field-aligned (parallel) viscosity. Heat-viscosity current
contributions are most significant in the edge plasma where the
collisionality is high enough for fluid closures to remain valid.

items.name: toroidal_coordinate_of_neutron_detector
items.description:
Toroidal coordinate of a neutron detector is the angular location of the
detector's geometric center about the machine symmetry axis in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Toroidal coordinate of a neutron detector is the angular coordinate of the
detector's geometric center about the machine symmetry axis in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R},
\hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$. Here $R$ is the major-radius coordinate, $\phi$ is
the toroidal angle, and $Z$ is the vertical-height coordinate.

For a detector center whose projection onto the plane perpendicular to
$\hat{Z}$ has Cartesian coordinates $x_c$ and $y_c$ in the right-handed
Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis, with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$ and
$\phi=0$ along $+\hat{x}$, the toroidal coordinate is

$$
\phi_\mathrm{n} = \operatorname{atan2}(y_c, x_c)
$$

where $\phi_\mathrm{n}$ is the toroidal coordinate of the neutron detector,
and $x_c$ and $y_c$ are the Cartesian coordinates of the detector geometric
center projected onto the plane perpendicular to $\hat{Z}$.

This quantity applies specifically to a neutron detector and to the point
representing its geometric center. The aggregation convention is none: it
denotes one detector center, not an average, sum, or representative angle
over several detectors; it is geometrically undefined for a center on the
symmetry axis, where no toroidal direction is selected.

It is not a detector orientation, angular extent, line-of-sight direction,
or the toroidal coordinate of an aperture or other component. It specializes
the generic [toroidal coordinate of a
detector](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_detector) to neutron detectors and is
distinct from [toroidal coordinate of an
aperture](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_aperture), which refers to an
aperture's own geometric center.

Sign convention: Positive when the detector geometric center is displaced in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, counter-clockwise when
viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$.

items.name: toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Signed nitrogen-ion fluid velocity component along the geometric toroidal
direction, evaluated at the radial location of the internal transport
barrier.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the signed nitrogen-ion fluid velocity component along the
geometric toroidal direction, evaluated at the radial location of the
internal transport barrier.

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{N}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{N}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{N}}$ is the nitrogen-ion fluid velocity and
$\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the geometric toroidal unit vector in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame; $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity represents directed nitrogen-ion flow at the barrier location,
not the total speed or radial and poloidal velocity components. It follows
the same component definition as [toroidal neon velocity at the internal
transport
barrier](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier), with
nitrogen as the species.

Sign convention: Positive when the nitrogen-ion flow has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: fast_ion_pressure
items.description:
Kinetic pressure tensor of the suprathermal ion population at a plasma
location, summed over all ion species and charge states and excluding the
Maxwellian thermal ion contribution.
items.documentation:
Fast-ion pressure is the kinetic pressure tensor of the suprathermal ion
population, defined through the second central velocity moment of the
fast-ion distribution function. It is summed over all ion species and all
charge states present in that suprathermal population, so it is the
charge-state-summed aggregate of [fast-ion charge-state
pressure](name:fast_ion_charge_state_pressure). It excludes the Maxwellian
thermal ion contribution represented by [thermal ion
pressure](name:thermal_ion_pressure).

The tensor is defined as the species and charge-state sum of the second
central velocity moment:

$$
\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{\alpha,q} m_\alpha \int (\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{\alpha q}) \otimes (\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{\alpha q})\, f_{\alpha q,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\, d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-ion pressure tensor,
$\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\alpha$ indexes ion species, $q$ indexes charge
state, $m_\alpha$ is the ion mass for species $\alpha$, $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{\alpha q}$ is the mean velocity of the
corresponding fast-ion subpopulation, $f_{\alpha q,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the
suprathermal distribution function whose velocity-space integral gives
number density, $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and $\otimes$
denotes the dyadic product.

The tensor may be anisotropic. The scalar fast-ion contribution entering the
isotropic [ion pressure](name:ion_pressure) is the trace pressure
$p_{\mathrm{fast}}=\operatorname{Tr}\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{fast}}/3$; for a
gyrotropic distribution in the local right-handed field-aligned basis
$(\hat{e}_1,\hat{e}_2,\hat{b})$, with $\hat{e}_1 \times \hat{e}_2=\hat{b}$
and $\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$, this is
$p_{\mathrm{fast}}=(P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}+2P_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}})/3$.
Here $P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}$ and $P_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}}$ are the
normal stresses parallel and perpendicular to the local magnetic-field
direction; related directional quantities include [parallel total fast-ion
pressure](name:parallel_total_fast_ion_pressure), [perpendicular total
fast-ion pressure](name:perpendicular_total_fast_ion_pressure), [parallel
fast-ion pressure](name:parallel_fast_ion_pressure), and [perpendicular
fast-ion pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_ion_pressure). The scalar
fast-ion contribution combines with the thermal contribution in total ion
pressure when the same population aggregation is used.

items.name: parallel_electron_velocity
items.description:
Signed projection of the electron-fluid bulk flow along the local magnetic
field, distinct from the random velocity spread associated with thermal
motion.
items.documentation:
The parallel electron velocity is the component of the local electron-fluid
bulk velocity along the magnetic-field direction. It describes directed
electron motion, including in the edge plasma, rather than random thermal
motion.

The defining projection is:

$$
v_{e\parallel}=\mathbf v_e\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}
$$

where $v_{e\parallel}$ is the parallel electron velocity, $\mathbf v_e$ is
the [electron velocity](name:electron_velocity), and $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is
the unit vector along the local magnetic field. The projection is defined
where the magnetic field is nonzero.

The electron-fluid velocity is the number-weighted mean over the local
electron velocity distribution; no spatial or flux-surface averaging is
implied. Its parallel component is not the total flow speed, a perpendicular
velocity component, a particle flux, or a thermal velocity spread.

Unlike [parallel plasma velocity](name:parallel_plasma_velocity), which
projects the mass-weighted bulk flow of all contributing plasma species,
this quantity projects only the electron-fluid flow.

Sign convention: Positive when the electron-fluid bulk motion has a
component along the local magnetic-field direction.

items.name: neutron_source_rate_due_to_beam_beam_fusion
items.description:
Neutron source rate due to beam-beam fusion is the volume-integrated rate at
which neutrons are produced by fusion reactions between energetic ions from
beam populations in the plasma. It is generic with respect to the
neutron-producing reaction channel.
items.documentation:
Neutron source rate due to beam-beam fusion is the plasma-volume-integrated
production rate of neutrons from fusion reactions in which both reacting
ions belong to energetic beam populations. The quantity fixes the fusion
product to neutrons while leaving the neutron-producing reaction channel to
be specified by more specific child names.

It is defined from the local volumetric neutron production rate density by

$$
R_n^{\mathrm{bb}} = \int_{V_p} s_n^{\mathrm{bb}}(\mathbf{x})\, dV
$$

where $R_n^{\mathrm{bb}}$ is the neutron source rate due to beam-beam
fusion, $s_n^{\mathrm{bb}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local volumetric neutron
production rate density from beam-beam fusion at position $\mathbf{x}$,
$V_p$ is the plasma volume, and $dV$ is an element of that volume.

The scope is restricted to neutron-producing fusion reactions between pairs
of energetic beam ions in the plasma. The aggregation convention is
integration over the plasma volume; this parent does not by itself impose a
sum over different isotope reaction channels.

This quantity excludes neutron production from beam-thermal and
thermal-thermal fusion reactions, and excludes source rates of charged
fusion products or photons. It is a neutron count-rate quantity, not the
fusion power, absorbed power, or particle energy carried by the products.

A channel-specific child such as [deuterium-deuterium neutron source rate
due to beam-beam
fusion](name:deuterium_deuterium_neutron_source_rate_due_to_beam_beam_fusion)
fixes the reacting isotope pair while preserving the same neutron-product
and beam-beam-reaction meaning. The broader [source rate due to beam-beam
fusion](name:source_rate_due_to_beam_beam_fusion), when used, allows the
produced fusion species to vary; this name is its neutron-product
specialization.

items.name: volume_averaged_oxygen_density
items.description:
Volume-averaged oxygen density is the spatial mean of the local oxygen
number density, summed over all charge states from neutral O0 through fully
stripped O8+, over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux
surface.
items.documentation:
The volume-averaged oxygen density is the volume mean of the local oxygen
number density—summed over all charge states from neutral O$^0$ through
fully stripped O$^{8+}$—within the confined plasma volume bounded by the
last closed flux surface. It characterizes the total oxygen impurity
inventory per confined plasma volume, independent of how that oxygen is
distributed inside the boundary.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle n_\mathrm{O} \rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{LCFS}} \int_{V_\mathrm{LCFS}} n_\mathrm{O}(\mathbf{r})\, dV
$$

where $\langle n_\mathrm{O} \rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged oxygen
density, $V_\mathrm{LCFS}$ is the confined plasma volume enclosed by the
last closed flux surface, $dV$ is a volume element, and
$n_\mathrm{O}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local [oxygen
density](name:oxygen_density), with $n_\mathrm{O}=\sum_{Z=0}^{8}
n_{\mathrm{O}^{Z+}}$.

This quantity differs from
[line_averaged_oxygen_density](name:line_averaged_oxygen_density), which is
a chord mean rather than a confined-volume mean. It is a charge-state-summed
species density and must not be interpreted as an ionic-only density that
excludes neutral oxygen.

items.name: turn_count_of_toroidal_field_coil
items.description:
Total winding count assigned to one toroidal-field coil, with fractional
values allowed for partial connections that do not make complete turns.
items.documentation:
The turn count is the total number of conductor windings assigned to a
single toroidal-field coil. It represents the winding multiplicity used in
generating the coil's toroidal magnetic field, including fractional
contributions when the represented connection contains partial turns.

The quantity is non-negative and aggregates all winding turns belonging to
that one coil. It is not an average, a count of discrete coil modules, or a
signed orientation parameter; fractional values describe partial connections
rather than a separate type of turn.

At fixed coil geometry and winding current, the magnetic-field contribution
scales with the turn count. The signed direction is supplied by the [current
of a toroidal-field coil](name:current_of_toroidal_field_coil), whereas this
quantity supplies the winding multiplicity. It is distinct from the [count
of toroidal-field coils](name:count_of_toroidal_field_coil), which counts
discrete coil modules, and from the [effective turn count of a passive
loop](name:effective_turn_count_of_passive_loop), which represents signed
equivalent windings for passive-loop electromagnetic coupling. The analogous
[turn count of a correction coil](name:turn_count_of_correction_coil)
applies to a different coil class.

items.name: counter_passing_fast_current_density
items.description:
Electric current density contributed by counter-passing fast particles on
guiding-center orbits, excluding thermal and compensating return-current
contributions.
items.documentation:
Electric current density contributed by fast particles classified as
counter-passing guiding-center orbits, excluding thermal and compensating
return-current contributions. It represents the charged fast-particle
contribution to the local plasma current rather than the total plasma
current.

The current density is the first velocity moment of the selected
fast-particle distributions:

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{cp,fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_a q_a \int_{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{cp}}} \mathbf{v}\, f_a(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $a$ identifies an included fast-particle
species or charge state, $q_a$ is its particle charge, $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity, $f_a$ is its phase-space distribution, and
$\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{cp}}$ selects the counter-passing fast-particle
population. It is an orbit-resolved member of the broader [fast current
density](name:fast_current_density) family; [co-passing fast current
density](name:co_passing_fast_current_density) represents the corresponding
co-passing class. A toroidal, flux-surface-averaged specialization is
[toroidal counter-passing fast current
density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_current_density).

Sign convention: Positive when each resolved component points along the
corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ basis; the toroidal component is positive toward increasing
$\phi$.

items.name: toroidal_iron_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of ionized iron at the magnetic
axis, directed along increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the charge-state-aggregated toroidal bulk-flow velocity of
ionized iron evaluated at the magnetic axis. It is the
number-density-weighted mean of the iron-ion fluid velocities, excluding
neutral iron.

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}}(\mathrm{axis}) = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}(\mathrm{axis})\,v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}(\mathrm{axis})}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}(\mathrm{axis})}
$$

Here $q$ indexes the included positive iron-ion charge states,
$n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}$ is the corresponding ion number density, and
$v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}$ is its toroidal velocity component in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame; the velocity is in m s$^{-1}$
and the density is in m$^{-3}$. The weighting is over charge states, so this
is an intensive mean rather than a sum of velocities. It is the
magnetic-axis counterpart of [toroidal iron velocity at the internal
transport
barrier](name:toroidal_iron_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier) and
follows the same aggregation principle as [toroidal deuterium velocity at
the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).

Sign convention: Positive when the iron bulk flow has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: pressure_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Kinetic plasma pressure evaluated at the fitted core-side shoulder of the
H-mode edge transport barrier, including population-specific and total
pressure contributions.
items.documentation:
Kinetic pressure at the pedestal top is the scalar stress associated with
random particle motion at the fitted core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge
transport barrier. It may describe a selected plasma population or the
aggregate of the populations included in the plasma pressure.

The scalar pressure is defined from the kinetic pressure tensor by

$$
p = \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{Tr}(\mathbf{P})
$$

where $p$ is the scalar kinetic pressure, $\mathbf{P}$ is the kinetic
pressure tensor, and $\operatorname{Tr}$ is the tensor trace. For a
specified population, $\mathbf{P}$ is that population's partial-pressure
tensor; the total plasma pressure is the sum of the partial pressures
included in the aggregation.

This quantity is restricted to the pedestal-top location, namely the fitted
core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, rather than a
pressure value at an arbitrary point or across the entire edge region. A
population-specific instance such as [electron pressure at the pedestal
top](name:electron_pressure_at_pedestal_top) represents only the electron
partial-pressure contribution and is therefore distinct from the total
plasma pressure. The quantity is pressure itself, not the electron
temperature or a dimensionless beta formed by normalizing pressure to
magnetic-field energy.

items.name: toroidal_flux_coordinate
items.description:
Toroidal flux coordinate is a non-negative, radius-like magnetic-surface
label derived from enclosed toroidal magnetic flux using a positive
reference vacuum toroidal field.
items.documentation:
Toroidal flux coordinate

The coordinate is defined by

$$\rho_{\mathrm{tor}} = \sqrt{\Phi/(\pi B_0)}$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal flux coordinate, $\Phi$ is the
non-negative toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by the flux surface, and $B_0$
is the positive reference vacuum toroidal magnetic-field strength at the
specified reference major radius.

The definition applies to any nested magnetic flux surface, without
restriction to a boundary, transport barrier, or mode-center locus. Each
surface carries a single label; this coordinate is neither a flux-surface
average nor a region integral and need not equal the surface's geometric
minor radius.

The [magnetic-axis value](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_of_magnetic_axis) is
zero because the enclosed toroidal flux vanishes there. With the same
reference field used throughout, dividing the coordinate by its
[plasma-boundary value](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_plasma_boundary)
gives the [normalized toroidal flux
coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate), which is zero at the
magnetic axis and one at that boundary.

items.name: magnetic_vector_potential
items.description:
Vector field whose curl gives the magnetic induction, gage-dependent but
physically central to canonical momentum, gyrokinetic, and
magnetohydrodynamic formulations of magnetized plasmas.
items.documentation:
The magnetic vector potential $\mathbf{A}$ is a gage-dependent vector field
characterizing the electromagnetic state of a plasma. It enters fundamental
physics through the canonical particle momentum $\mathbf{p} = m\mathbf{v} +
q\mathbf{A}$, where $m$ is particle mass and $q$ is particle charge, and it
governs inductive electromagnetic effects in both equilibrium and perturbed
plasma states.

The defining relation connecting $\mathbf{A}$ to the magnetic induction
$\mathbf{B}$ is:

$$
\mathbf{B} = \nabla \times \mathbf{A}
$$

where $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic induction. Only the curl of $\mathbf{A}$
is directly physical; the vector potential itself is gage dependent. Its
time derivative contributes to the inductive electric field via
$\mathbf{E}_\mathrm{ind} = -\partial\mathbf{A}/\partial t$, which is central
to Faraday's law in electromagnetic plasma models.

Specific projections serve distinct physical roles. The field-aligned
component $A_\parallel = \mathbf{A} \cdot \hat{b}$, where $\hat{b}$ is the
equilibrium field unit vector, governs Alfvénic dynamics and is the
component retained in gyrokinetic and reduced-MHD formulations; its
normalized perturbed amplitude is used in eigenmode studies. Cylindrical
components in the right-handed $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame — radial, toroidal, and
vertical — are natural for equilibrium and MHD calculations, while the
poloidal projection in flux coordinates $(\psi, \theta, \phi)$ arises in
neoclassical transport analyzes. In vacuum regions, $\mathbf{A}$ is
generated solely by external coil currents, with no plasma-current
contribution.

items.name: polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam
items.description:
Signed ratio of the minor to major semiaxes of the polarization ellipse of a
polarimeter beam after propagation through magnetized plasma. It describes
the beam's post-propagation transverse polarization state, not the incident
state or the ellipse orientation.
items.documentation:
Signed ratio of the minor to major semiaxes of the polarization ellipse of a
polarimeter beam after propagation through magnetized plasma is the
ellipticity of that beam. It characterizes the relative electric-field
semiamplitudes of the post-propagation transverse polarization ellipse.

The ellipticity is defined by

$$
\varepsilon = \frac{b}{a}
$$

where $\varepsilon$ is the polarization ellipticity, $a$ is the major-axis
semiamplitude of the electric-field polarization ellipse, and $b$ is the
signed minor-axis semiamplitude of that ellipse. The magnitude satisfies
$|\varepsilon| \leq 1$.

This quantity applies to the polarimeter beam after it has traversed the
magnetized plasma and is therefore distinct from the [initial polarization
ellipticity](name:initial_polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam). It
is a polarization-shape parameter and excludes the orientation of the
ellipse; rotation of that orientation is represented by the [Faraday
angle](name:faraday_angle). The quantity refers to a single beam
polarization state, with no aggregation over distinct beam paths.

Magnetized-plasma birefringence can transform the [initial polarization
ellipticity](name:initial_polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam) into
this post-propagation ellipticity by changing the polarization ellipse
during propagation; that change is distinct from Faraday rotation of the
ellipse orientation.

Sign convention: Positive when the electric-field vector rotates in a
right-handed sense about the beam-propagation direction.

items.name: ion_charge_state_torque_density
items.description:
Local vector rate of net angular-momentum transfer per unit volume for a
specified ion charge state, retaining the complete torque-vector direction.
items.documentation:
Torque density for a specified ion charge state is the local vector rate at
which angular momentum is transferred to or from that ion population per
unit volume. It retains the complete torque-vector direction rather than
selecting a toroidal or other component, and is a charge-state-resolved
instance of [torque_density](name:torque_density).

The defining relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau} = \left(\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}}{\partial t}\right)_{\mathrm{transfer}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}$ is the torque-density vector, $\boldsymbol{\ell}$
is the angular-momentum density of the specified ion charge state, and $t$
is time. The transfer term represents the net angular-momentum exchange
included by this unqualified quantity.

The selected plasma content is one specified ion species in one specified
ionization state. The quantity is local, net over the applicable transfer
mechanisms, and not summed over other ion species or charge states. It
excludes any restriction to a particular orbit class or spatial component.

Unlike [ion_torque_density](name:ion_torque_density), which aggregates over
all ion species and charge states, this quantity resolves the selected ion
charge state. Its toroidal component is represented by
[toroidal_ion_charge_state_torque_density](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_torque_density),
while the present quantity retains the full vector.

Sign convention: Positive when the torque vector points along the
corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ basis; its toroidal component is positive when it increases angular
momentum in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: tritium_density_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Number density of the tritium species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for tritium ions at the sheath entrance
immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary.
items.documentation:
Number density of the tritium species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the tritium-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local tritium ion number density is defined by the positive-ion count:

$$
n_T = n_{T^+} = \frac{dN_T}{dV}
$$

where $n_T$ is the tritium ion number density, $n_{T^+}$ is the number
density of singly ionized tritium ions, $N_T$ is the number of tritium ions
in a small plasma volume, and $V$ is that plasma volume as its center
approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side.

This quantity applies to the tritium ion population immediately adjacent to
the divertor target and is summed over all positive atomic ionization
states; for tritium, the included atomic ion is $T^+$. Neutral tritium atoms
and molecules, electrons, deuterium ions, and other ion species are
excluded.

It specializes [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target)
by selecting only tritium ions. Unlike
[deuterium_tritium_density_at_divertor_target](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_divertor_target),
it does not aggregate the deuterium and tritium fuel-ion populations.

items.name: current_of_passive_structure
items.description:
Current in a passive structure is the signed rate of conventional charge
transport circulating toroidally through one axisymmetric member.
items.documentation:
Current of passive structure

The current $I$ is defined by

$$
I = \int_S \mathbf{J}\cdot\hat{\phi}\,dS
$$

where $S$ is the member's full poloidal cross-section, $\mathbf{J}$ is the
[conventional electric current density](name:current_density), and $dS$ is a
surface-area element. The vector $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in
the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity integrates current density over one member's cross-section; it
is not a sum over all passive structures and excludes plasma and active-coil
currents. When the specified member is a passive loop, it equals the
[current of that loop](name:current_of_passive_loop).

Sign convention: Positive when conventional electric current flows in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: plasma_magnetic_vector_potential
items.description:
Plasma-associated magnetic vector potential whose curl gives the
corresponding magnetic induction, including perturbations relative to a
reference state in a gage-dependent vector representation.
items.documentation:
The plasma magnetic vector potential is the gage-dependent vector field
associated with the magnetic field in the plasma. It retains the complete
vector quantity rather than selecting a radial, poloidal, toroidal,
vertical, or field-parallel component.

The defining relation connecting the vector potential to its associated
magnetic induction is:

$$
\mathbf{B}_{\rm pl} = \nabla \times \mathbf{A}_{\rm pl}
$$

where $\mathbf{A}_{\rm pl}$ is the plasma-associated magnetic vector
potential, $\mathbf{B}_{\rm pl}$ is the corresponding plasma-associated
magnetic induction, and $\nabla \times$ is the spatial curl operator. Only
the curl is directly field-defining; $\mathbf{A}_{\rm pl}$ itself depends on
the chosen gage.

This parent denotes the full unprojected plasma-associated vector potential
across equilibrium and perturbed states. It retains its radial, poloidal,
toroidal, vertical, and field-parallel components as a vector, without
component averaging, Fourier selection, or magnitude formation. The concrete
[perturbed plasma magnetic vector
potential](name:perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential) represents the
change in this quantity relative to a reference state.

The plasma-associated quantity is distinct from the external-source-only
[vacuum magnetic vector potential](name:vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential).
Together with the broader [magnetic vector
potential](name:magnetic_vector_potential), it provides the
plasma-associated contribution to the magnetic-field description; the vacuum
quantity instead excludes plasma-current contributions.

items.name: implicit_electron_energy_source_rate
items.description:
Implicit electron energy source rate is the signed coefficient whose product
with the energy equation's primary quantity gives the implicitly treated
electron energy source or sink.
items.documentation:
Implicit electron energy source rate is the multiplicative coefficient of
the implicitly treated part of a decomposed electron energy source term. It
specifies a source or sink contribution proportional to the primary quantity
of the electron energy transport equation.

The source decomposition is:

$$
F_{e,W} = F_{e,W}^{\mathrm{exp}} + S_{e,W}^{\mathrm{imp}} u_e
$$

where $F_{e,W}$ is the complete source term in the chosen electron energy
equation, $F_{e,W}^{\mathrm{exp}}$ is its additive explicit contribution,
$S_{e,W}^{\mathrm{imp}}$ is the implicit electron energy source rate, and
$u_e$ is the equation's primary quantity. The subscripts $e$ and $W$
identify the electron population and energy channel. In a temperature-based
formulation, $u_e$ is electron temperature; all source terms must correspond
to that same formulation.

This coefficient applies to the electron energy channel and is neither the
additive explicit source nor the complete source term. It has the same
decomposition role as the [implicit ion energy source
