rate](name:implicit_ion_energy_source_rate), but applies to electrons rather
than ions. Unlike the [implicit electron particle source
rate](name:implicit_electron_particle_source_rate), which multiplies
electron number density in particle balance, it multiplies the primary
quantity of the energy equation.

Sign convention: Positive when multiplication by a positive primary quantity
gives an energy gain for electrons; negative when it gives an energy loss.

items.name: launched_wave_duration
items.description:
Duration of a single frequency sweep during which a probing electromagnetic
wave is launched.
items.documentation:
Launched wave duration is the time interval of one complete swept-frequency
launch of a probing electromagnetic wave. It is defined by the start and end
times of the same launched-wave sweep, independent of how any received
signal is analyzed.

For a sweep beginning at $t_{\mathrm{start}}$ and ending at
$t_{\mathrm{end}}$, the launched wave duration is:

$$
\Delta t_{\mathrm{lw}} = t_{\mathrm{end}} - t_{\mathrm{start}}
$$

where $\Delta t_{\mathrm{lw}}$ is the launched wave duration, and
$t_{\mathrm{start}}$ and $t_{\mathrm{end}}$ are the sweep start and end
times, all measured in seconds.

The corresponding launched frequency during this interval is described by
launched_wave_frequency. This quantity specifies only the duration of the
complete sweep; it does not define the detailed frequency waveform, dwell
time at individual frequencies, received-wave interval, or signal-analysis
interval.

items.name: external_loop_voltage
items.description:
Electromotive-force contribution to the plasma loop voltage caused by
changing externally generated poloidal magnetic flux, including flux linked
through active coils and passive conducting structures.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the inductive electromotive-force contribution to the
plasma loop voltage produced by time-varying poloidal magnetic flux
generated by active coil circuits and magnetically coupled passive
conducting structures. It excludes resistive voltage drops and other
non-inductive contributions.

The contribution is defined by Faraday's law:

$$
V_{\mathrm{ext}}(t) = -\frac{d\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(t)}{dt}
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is the externally generated poloidal magnetic
flux linked by the considered toroidal plasma circuit and $t$ is time. It
contributes to the total [loop voltage at the plasma
boundary](name:loop_voltage_at_plasma_boundary); currents in passive
conductors are represented by the linked-flux response of structures such as
those described by [current of passive
structure](name:current_of_passive_structure).

Sign convention: Positive when the induced electromotive force has a
positive line integral in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid
items.description:
Nonnegative major-radius location of the geometric centroid of one ferritic
element in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the radial coordinate of the geometric centroid of one
ferritic element, locating that centroid by its distance from the toroidal
symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Here $R$
is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The centroid radial coordinate is defined by

$$
R_c = \sqrt{x_c^2+y_c^2}
$$

where $R_c$ is the radial coordinate of the ferritic-element centroid, and
$x_c$ and $y_c$ are its Cartesian coordinates in the right-handed Cartesian
$(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis, with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$.

This quantity applies independently to each ferritic element and is not
summed or averaged over elements. It is distinct from the [radial outline
coordinate of a ferritic element](name:radial_outline_of_ferritic_element),
which locates contour points, and from the [vertical coordinate of a
ferritic-element centroid](name:z_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid),
which provides the centroid's $Z$ coordinate. It is the
ferritic-element-centroid specialization of the general [radial
coordinate](name:radial_coordinate).

items.name: fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface
items.description:
Cumulative wave power absorbed by the fast (non-thermal) ion population
within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
The fast-ion power at inside flux surface is the running volume integral of
wave power deposited into the fast (non-thermal) ion population, giving the
radial distribution of enclosed fast-ion wave absorption. It is the fast-ion
component of the more general
[ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface),
separating non-thermal ion energy absorption from the corresponding bulk
thermal-ion contribution.

The quantity is the volume integral of the fast-ion wave-power density
$p_f(\mathbf{r})$ over the plasma domain $V(\psi)$ enclosed by the magnetic
flux surface labeled $\psi$:

$$
P_f(\psi) = \int_{V(\psi)} p_f(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $P_f(\psi)$ is the fast-ion power at inside flux surface, $p_f$ is the
fast-ion volumetric wave-power density, $\mathbf{r}$ is position in physical
space, $dV$ is the differential volume element, $V(\psi)$ is the enclosed
plasma volume, and $\psi$ is the chosen magnetic flux-surface label.

The scope is the plasma volume inside the selected closed magnetic flux
surface and the fast, non-thermal ion population in that volume. Because
this is an extensive population quantity, it is summed over the represented
fast-ion species and over all their charge states; the charge-state-resolved
counterpart is
[fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface).
It excludes wave energy deposited into the bulk thermal-ion population,
represented by
[thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface),
and excludes electron heating and wave power not absorbed by fast ions. For
the same flux-surface label,
[ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface) is
the sum of this fast-ion contribution and the thermal-ion contribution.

items.name: thickness_of_antenna_strap
items.description:
Thickness of an ICRH antenna strap is the full, non-negative extent of the
strap conductor cross-section perpendicular to the central segment of the
strap rectangle in the thick-line geometric approximation. It is distinct
from strap width, height, and length.
items.documentation:
Thickness of an ICRH antenna strap is the full, non-negative extent of the
strap conductor cross-section in the direction perpendicular to the central
segment of the strap rectangle in the thick-line geometric approximation. It
is a geometric length of the strap conductor, not an oriented displacement.

For a strap conductor cross-section $C$ and a unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$
along the modeled thickness direction, the thickness $t$ is the range of
projected positions:

$$
t = \max_{\mathbf{r}\in C}\left(\mathbf{r}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}\right) - \min_{\mathbf{r}\in C}\left(\mathbf{r}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}\right)
$$

where $t$ is the thickness of the antenna strap, $C$ is the conductor
cross-section, $\mathbf{r}$ is a position vector for a point of that
cross-section, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is a unit vector in the cross-section
perpendicular to the central segment of the strap rectangle.

The scope is a single ICRH antenna strap represented by the thick-line
strap-rectangle geometry. The aggregation convention is the complete
max-minus-min extent over the conductor cross-section along the modeled
thickness direction; it is not an average thickness, a local surface
separation, a half-thickness, or a signed offset.

Thickness is an independent strap-geometry extent that complements the width
of the antenna strap, [height of the antenna
strap](name:height_of_antenna_strap), and length of the antenna strap. Those
quantities describe separate geometric extents of the same strap rather than
projections along the thickness direction.

items.name: counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure
items.description:
One-third of the kinetic-stress trace carried by suprathermal particles on
untrapped orbits whose orbit-averaged toroidal motion opposes the plasma
current, including directed-motion contributions.
items.documentation:
Counter-passing fast-particle pressure is one-third of the kinetic-stress
trace carried by suprathermal particles on counter-passing guiding-center
orbits. These particles are untrapped and have orbit-averaged toroidal
motion opposite to the plasma current.

For a nonrelativistic species, the local pressure is defined by the
restricted second velocity moment:

$$
p_{s,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{m_s}{3}\int_{\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{cp}}(\mathbf{x})} |\mathbf{v}|^2 f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{s,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the counter-passing
fast-particle pressure, $s$ labels the specified particle species, $m_s$ is
its particle mass, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity, $f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is its suprathermal distribution
function, $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{cp}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the velocity-space
region belonging to counter-passing orbits at that position, and $d^3v$ is
the velocity-space volume element.

The velocity moment does not subtract the population mean velocity, so
directed motion contributes alongside random motion. Only the suprathermal
counter-passing population is included; thermal particles, [co-passing fast
particles](name:co_passing_fast_particle_pressure), and [trapped fast
particles](name:trapped_fast_particle_pressure) are excluded. Contributions
from multiple represented fast-particle populations of the specified species
add linearly, rather than forming a density-weighted mean; no sum over
different species is implied.

The definition retains local spatial variation. A flux-surface average
averages this same local moment and is not intrinsic to the quantity's
definition.

This is the counter-passing orbit-class contribution to [fast-particle
pressure](name:fast_particle_pressure). Its component relationship is
$p_{s,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{fast}}=(p_{\parallel,s}+2p_{\perp,s})/3$, where
$p_{\parallel,s}$ is the [parallel counter-passing fast-particle
pressure](name:parallel_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure) and
$p_{\perp,s}$ is the [perpendicular counter-passing fast-particle
pressure](name:perpendicular_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure),
averaged over the two transverse directions relative to the local magnetic
field. The trace combines these components without requiring them to be
equal; it is neither a single directional component nor an assumption of an
isotropic distribution.

items.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
items.description:
Volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density divided by volume-averaged
electron density for the combined deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species,
treating deuterium and tritium as one effective species.
items.documentation:
Volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density divided by volume-averaged
electron density for the combined deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species,
treating deuterium and tritium as one effective species, is the
electron-density-normalized abundance of that fuel species. It compares the
fuel-ion population with the electron population after each density is
averaged over the same plasma volume.

The ratio is defined by:

$$
\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{DT}/e} = \frac{\langle n_{\mathrm{DT}} \rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
$$

where $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{DT}/e}$ is this ratio, $\langle n_{\mathrm{DT}}
\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged deuterium-tritium
density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density), $\langle n_e
\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $n_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the
local number density of the combined deuterium-tritium effective species,
$n_e$ is the local electron number density, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_V$
denotes averaging over the common plasma volume $V$.

The scope is the plasma volume common to numerator and denominator; the
value is a ratio of two volume averages, not the volume average of a
pointwise density ratio. The numerator is a species-level extensive density
for the effective deuterium-tritium fuel species and is summed over all
charge states before averaging. It includes only that fuel species and
excludes helium ash, impurity ions, and separate isotope-composition ratios
such as the [tritium-to-deuterium density
ratio](name:ratio_of_tritium_density_to_deuterium_density).

Equivalently, this quantity is the [volume-averaged deuterium-tritium
density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density) normalized by the
[volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density);
it is a normalized ratio, not a derivative of either density. When the
combined deuterium-tritium density is resolved into deuterium and tritium
contributions over the same volume and denominator, it equals the sum of the
[volume-averaged deuterium-to-electron density
ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density)
and the [volume-averaged tritium-to-electron density
ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

items.name: neutral_state_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Dimensionless coefficient that limits the particle flux carried by a
specified neutral state by scaling its collisionless free-streaming bound.
items.documentation:
The dimensionless particle flux-limiter coefficient for a specified neutral
state controls the admissible particle flux in the density equation by
scaling its collisionless free-streaming bound. It applies to thermal and
nonthermal particles belonging to that neutral state.

The limiting relation is

$$
|\Gamma_s| \leq \alpha_s\,\Gamma_{\mathrm{fs},s}
$$

where $\Gamma_s$ is the particle flux of the specified neutral state,
$\alpha_s$ is this flux-limiter coefficient, and $\Gamma_{\mathrm{fs},s}$ is
the collisionless free-streaming bound for the same state.

The coefficient is specific to the named neutral state and applies to the
total particle-flux contribution from its thermal and nonthermal
populations; it is not summed over different neutral states. It limits
particle transport only and does not represent the separate momentum-flux
limitation described by [neutral momentum flux limiter
coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).

This quantity is the neutral-state specialization of the broader [particle
flux limiter coefficient](name:particle_flux_limiter_coefficient). The
corresponding [ion-state particle flux limiter
coefficient](name:ion_state_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient) applies the
same limiting relationship to a specified ion state rather than to a neutral
state.
